item.title: 49ers-Raiders: DeForest Buckner's impact? Cousins to Bowers a problem?
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers makes a one-handed catch for a touchdown over New York Jets defensive back Jarvis Brownlee Jr. on Nov. 1. (Rusty Jones/Associated Press) The San Francisco 49ers return to the field on Sunday after their bye week to host the Las Vegas Raiders. Kyle Shanahan 's 49ers (6-1) are looking to bounce back from a 29-20 letdown in Atlanta, their first loss of the season, and the trade deadline looms on Tuesday. We asked staff writers Eric Branch and Harrison Rich and columnist Ann Killion to weigh in on some key questions ahead of the matchup against the Raiders (4-4). How much of an impact will the acquisition of defensive tackle DeForest Buckner have on the 49ers? Where would you rank this in the pantheon of their midseason trades in recent years? Eric Branch: It obviously ranks below the 2022 Christian McCaffrey blockbuster on the deadline Richter scale and it's not quite on par with the 2019 Emmanuel Sanders deal. At 32, Buckner is still an impact player (surprise: GM John Lynch maintains he's playing the best of his 11-year career), but, unlike the 2019 49ers' room that Sanders massively upgraded, the 49ers' banged-up defensive interior has been stouter than expected, largely thanks to the quick emergence of fourth-round rookie steal Gracen Halton. Ann Killion: We'll figure out where this trade ranks at the end of the season based on the results: If they get to a Super Bowl and win it and Buckner plays a role, it will be an all-timer. Even without knowing how the trade turns out, I like the move a lot. Buckner is still a really good player, he was miserable with the situation in Indianapolis, the Colts were having a fire-sale and he fits perfectly with the 49ers 2026 season theme of "getting the band back together." It was a no-brainer. Harrison Rich: This is no midseason move for prime McCaffrey, but it's certainly more aggressive than last season's deadline move for Keion White. Buckner is no longer at his peak. This is not the same player 49ers fans have fond memories of watching back in 2019, but he is still a good player at age 32, and his sheer presence will make life easier for the rest of the Niners defense. He will draw double teams, and fellow defensive linemen will receive more one-on-one opportunities. Buckner moves the needle, for sure, but it's hard to say this is the trade that puts the 49ers over the top in the postseason. The 49ers are still in the market for a wide receiver. How hard should they push to acquire a stopgap at the position, or should they seek a front-line wideout in case injuries to Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel turn out to be more severe than anticipated? Branch: Evans is clearly their most impactful wideout. He's 33, has been sidelined by Achilles tendinits since Oct. 19 and Lynch said this week there is "hope" that he can return to play in the "coming weeks" while invoking McCaffrey's 2024 bout with the same injury that sidelined him for eight games. Still, the 6-1 start means
item.content:encoded: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers makes a one-handed catch for a touchdown over New York Jets defensive back Jarvis Brownlee Jr. on Nov. 1. (Rusty Jones/Associated Press) The San Francisco 49ers return to the field on Sunday after their bye week to host the Las Vegas Raiders. Kyle Shanahan 's 49ers (6-1) are looking to bounce back from a 29-20 letdown in Atlanta, their first loss of the season, and the trade deadline looms on Tuesday. We asked staff writers Eric Branch and Harrison Rich and columnist Ann Killion to weigh in on some key questions ahead of the matchup against the Raiders (4-4). How much of an impact will the acquisition of defensive tackle DeForest Buckner have on the 49ers? Where would you rank this in the pantheon of their midseason trades in recent years? Eric Branch: It obviously ranks below the 2022 Christian McCaffrey blockbuster on the deadline Richter scale and it's not quite on par with the 2019 Emmanuel Sanders deal. At 32, Buckner is still an impact player (surprise: GM John Lynch maintains he's playing the best of his 11-year career), but, unlike the 2019 49ers' room that Sanders massively upgraded, the 49ers' banged-up defensive interior has been stouter than expected, largely thanks to the quick emergence of fourth-round rookie steal Gracen Halton. Ann Killion: We'll figure out where this trade ranks at the end of the season based on the results: If they get to a Super Bowl and win it and Buckner plays a role, it will be an all-timer. Even without knowing how the trade turns out, I like the move a lot. Buckner is still a really good player, he was miserable with the situation in Indianapolis, the Colts were having a fire-sale and he fits perfectly with the 49ers 2026 season theme of "getting the band back together." It was a no-brainer. Harrison Rich: This is no midseason move for prime McCaffrey, but it's certainly more aggressive than last season's deadline move for Keion White. Buckner is no longer at his peak. This is not the same player 49ers fans have fond memories of watching back in 2019, but he is still a good player at age 32, and his sheer presence will make life easier for the rest of the Niners defense. He will draw double teams, and fellow defensive linemen will receive more one-on-one opportunities. Buckner moves the needle, for sure, but it's hard to say this is the trade that puts the 49ers over the top in the postseason. The 49ers are still in the market for a wide receiver. How hard should they push to acquire a stopgap at the position, or should they seek a front-line wideout in case injuries to Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel turn out to be more severe than anticipated? Branch: Evans is clearly their most impactful wideout. He's 33, has been sidelined by Achilles tendinits since Oct. 19 and Lynch said this week there is "hope" that he can return to play in the "coming weeks" while invoking McCaffrey's 2024 bout with the same injury that sidelined him for eight games. Still, the 6-1 start means the 49ers don't have to panic to trade for a fill-in. And their failed pursuit of Vikings WR Jauan Jennings , which would have been a relatively low-wattage trade, suggests they are looking for more stopgap than superstar. Killion: They have to be in the market for a wide receiver, considering their dire situation. Evans is a superstar but he got hurt in mid-October and even if he returns, at 33 there's no guarantee he's going to stay healthy the rest of the way. The 49ers have a lot of receiver talent supposedly coming off injuries soon, but as we've learned too well with this team, injured players don't always bounce back the way the team hopes. There are some long, cold months ahead. Rich: Seek a difference-making wideout. This is the 49ers' best remaining chance, with a 6-1 record and relatively good health, to win a Super Bowl with this core. Receiver is the team's biggest need. You should let Evans rest as long as he needs to, as long as he's healthy in January. You can't rely on Samuel or Demarcus Robinson or rookie De'Zhaun Stribling , all coming off injuries, to get back to their preseason levels at this point. Go get a running mate for Evans and another weapon for Purdy, who has clearly been struggling to connect with his receivers as of late. The 49ers have had some struggles covering tight ends this year (Trey McBride, the Falcons group). Is there a concern that the Kirk Cousins to Brock Bowers combination could be a significant problem Sunday? Branch: The 49ers did allow their first two TDs to tight ends in the Week 7 loss in Atlanta, and McBride had nine catches for 75 yards in Week 3. Still, the presence of linebackers Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw is a big reason why the 49ers have actually been largely effective against tight ends: They are allowing six catches and 43.6 yards per game to the position. Like McBride, Bowers is good enough to inflate those numbers. He missed the first two regular-season games with a knee injury, but his per-game averages this season would translate to 116 catches for 1,550 yards and 14 TDs over 17 games. Killion: Sure it could be a problem. Cousins to Bowers will be defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' biggest concern. Bowers is the Raiders' biggest threat so he'll get a lot of attention and, like Harrison points out, the 49ers will be willing to see if someone else can beat them. It will be fun to see what Shanahan protege Klint Kubiak cooks up against his one-time mentor. Rich: The Cousins-to-Bowers connection is difficult for any opposing defense to contain. Cousins owns some of the best numbers among quarterbacks in 2026, and as Eric notes, Bowers has been on a tear. Bowers had two touchdowns last week against the Jets, and he reached the end zone in three of his prior five matchups. The 49ers might be best off doubling Bowers - or at least giving him extra attention - and forcing someone else to beat them. Prediction time. Who wins and why? Branch: Injuries will force the 49ers to trot out an underwhelming WR group for the second straight game after this crew's lack of production factored into their first loss of the season. The good news for the 49ers: They might be able to overwhelm the porous Raiders defense with Purdy, McCaffrey and Kittle doing nearly all the lifting. 49ers 27, Raiders 16 Killion: The 49ers got their bad loss out of the way two weeks ago, losing to Atlanta before the bye week, giving them a bad taste over their break. Now, they're rested and relaxed and ready for the final 10 games of the season. Shanahan is 6-1 after the bye week in the last seven years. 49ers 35, Raiders 20 Rich: A struggling 49ers offense against a struggling Raiders defense should make for an interesting matchup. Las Vegas has allowed at least 30 points in five straight weeks. The Rams put up 35 on them, and the Patriots scored 45. But this is a sneaky good offense led by Cousins. So if the Niners can't reach that 30-point mark at minimum, things could get dicey. 49ers 33, Raiders 24 Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Shenendehowa girls' volleyball continues Section 2 title streak
item.description: Shenendehowa celebrates after beating Saratoga in the Section 2, Class AAA finals on Friday, Nov. 6, in Saratoga, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) SARATOGA SPRINGS - The Shenendehowa girls' volleyball team boasts a powerhouse up front, with several weapons the Mustangs can call on to make an impact. In Friday's Section 2 Class AAA championship, Shenendehowa's potent offense was the focus once again as the top-seeded Mustangs swept past No. 2 Saratoga Springs in straight sets 25-13, 25-14, 25-16, at Saratoga Springs High School. "It makes it so fun because the defense doesn't really have one person to focus on," Shenendehowa coach Lori Kessler said. "They have to focus on three hitting options at all times, and running a 6-2 with two great setters, they're spreading it out. It's such a great part of our offense." Shenendehowa sophomores Melanie Tubbs and Claire Siska combined for 18 kills, junior Hadley Ennist added 10 kills and 11 assists, and senior Ava Los chipped in five kills. Shenendehowa, the top-ranked team in the state Class AAA poll, pushed its sectional title win streak to six with. The four most recent championships have come in Class AAA since the state expanded to a six-classification system. "It's a completely new team than what we've had in the past," Ennist said. "It's a ton of younger girls and some seniors. It's just such a big mix and honestly, we're doing a great job together. It's so fun to be able to play with such a variety of ages and abilities out there." Key moment Shenendehowa trailed 6-5 in the second set, but used a pair of runs to gain control. The Mustangs used a 7-0 spurt to grab a 12-6 lead, and Ennist set up sophomore Leah Alfandre for a kill to cap a 5-1 run which provided Shenendehowa its first double-digit lead of the set, 17-7. "Those were really big for us, especially in a game this competitive," Ennist said. "If you do get into a little bit of a rut, you still have so much time to come out of it, and I think we did a really great job of getting that lead." Star of the game Shenendehowa freshman setter Kyli Kessler, the coach's daughter, turned in a stellar all-around performance. Kessler finished with 19 assists, 12 service points, including a pair of aces, and nine digs. "She works hard year-round on her game," Lori Kessler said of her daughter. "I think that she really wanted to prove herself this season, and I think that her being surrounded by the girls, by the great passing and the great hitters, makes her job a little bit easier for her. But regardless, she's still an everyday hard worker that if something feels off, she's the first one out there that wants to fix it and make it better for everybody." Numbers to know 15: Digs Shenendehowa sophomore defensive specialist Avery Young recorded. 10: Kills Saratoga junior standout outside hitter Ali Sherman totaled. 6: Blocks Los made in the contest. item.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Finds Home With Reds Or Nats
item.description: Oct 5, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (13) is out on a batted ball during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game two of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Jazz Chisholm Jr. brings elite speed and power , but his time in New York faces an uncertain future. The Yankees’ second baseman posted a career-high 31 home runs in 2025, yet his consistency remains a major question mark. Fox Sports reports that his 1.7 wins above replacement (bWAR) and 97 OPS+ in 2026 likely cost him a long-term deal. Teams will pay for his talent, but they will not commit to a massive contract without proof of stability. A Fresh Start in Washington The Washington Nationals offer Chisholm a clear path to rebuild his value. Washington finished third in MLB in runs with 821 and slugged at .423 last season, showing they need more punch up the middle. While Nasim Nuñez led the National League with 49 stolen bases, he lacks the power Chisholm provides. The Nationals could use Chisholm to open 2027 as their starting second baseman and help fill the void left by trading Luis García Jr. and Curtis Mead. Chisholm’s move gives him a chance to play either middle infield spot, depending on how the team handles shortstop CJ Abrams. The Reds Need an Offensive Boost With only 75 wins, Cincinnati finished last in the National League Central and urgently needs improvement. MLB hits totaled 1,231 for the Reds, who also recorded the league’s lowest on-base percentage. Chisholm would give them a capable, impact left-handed hitter to balance the lineup. He would likely start at second base, pushing Matt McLain to the bench. McLain has been the primary second baseman for two years but hit a combined .204 during that stretch. Chisholm’s two-time All-Star status would be a massive upgrade for Terry Francona’s order. The market for Chisholm will depend on how teams view his 37.3 stolen bases per season since 2024. He showed he can hit for power, with 80 RBIs in 2025, a year in which he also posted 4.1 wins above replacement. Under Aaron Boone, the Yankees made the postseason eight times over nine years, yet they must determine whether Chisholm belongs in their future. ESPN notes that free agents will come off the board quickly before the league shuts down on Dec. 1.

item.title: What Carlos Alcaraz said to Taylor Fritz after eliminating him from ATP Finals contention
item.description: Taylor Fritz had two match points on Carlos Alcaraz on Friday in his Paris Masters quarterfinal. He had taken the first set in a marathon tiebreaker and had all of the momentum leading 5-3 in the second set. Then, as if a light switch went off, Alcaraz raised his level and got the crowd involved. Fritz needed the win to qualify for the ATP Finasl, but 2 hours and 45 minutes later, it was not to be as Alcaraz won the match in three sets, 6-7, 7-5, 6-3. The quality of the tennis was high, but many were sad for Fritz who came so close to making the ATP Finals in a year where he battled a knee injury that kept him out of the game for some time. Alcaraz was well aware of what was on the line for Fritz and was ready to talk about it when they met at the net after match point. MORE: Madison Keys, Taylor Fritz bared their souls in hearbreaking US Open press conferences Alcaraz apologized to Fritz Tennis – U.S. Open – Flushing Meadows, New York, United States – September 5, 2026 Taylor Fritz of the U.S. in action during his third round match against Argentina’s Francisco Cerundolo IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Robert Deutsch Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters (Reuters) The first Alcaraz said to Sinner was that he was sorry. Fritz smiled at him and said he was too good. Sportsmanship personified between two players who produced a high level of tennis in a grueling match. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Tennis TV (@tennistv) This loss will sting for Fritz, but he knows how to manage the emotional highs and lows of the game. The Alcaraz Magic Show continues 🪄 He saves multiple match points in the second set to defeat Fritz in Paris. #RolexParisMasters https://t.co/gYSabULmyc — Tennis Channel (@TennisChannel) November 6, 2026 MORE: What does Ben Shelton gain by hiring Carlos Alcaraz’s former coach? Tommy Paul also knocked out of ATP Finals Paul lost to Ben Shelton , who finishes the year as the top ranked American for the first time, in Paris ending his bid to make the ATP Finals. Year-end No.1 American men: 2021 – Taylor Fritz 2022 – Taylor Fritz 2023 – Taylor Fritz 2024 – Taylor Fritz 2025 – Taylor Fritz 2026 – Ben Shelton — Bastien Fachan (@BastienFachan) November 6, 2026 He seemed unbothered about the outcome, either way. His offseason plan was to go fishing . After an eleven month season and a post Wimbledon wedding to longtime girlfriend Paige Lorenze , Paul is ready for some downtime. Shelton and Frances Tiafoe are the American singles qualifiers for the ATP Finals in Turin. It is Tiafoe’s first time playing in the event which features the top eight players. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: SpaceX launches mystery mission for US Space Force in gorgeous sunset liftoff from California (photos)
item.description: null SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. The Falcon 9's first stage after its landing on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. Previous Booster 1095 missions GPS-III 8 | 6 Starlink missions USSF-432 was the 119th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, and the 14th national-security flight of the rocket so far this year. The vast majority of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 — more than 70% — have been devoted to building out the Starlink megaconstellation. SpaceX has also launched six other missions this year. Three were operational flights of the company's Falcon Heavy rocket, while the other three were test missions of its next-gen Starship vehicle. SpaceX plans to retire both the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy shortly after the fully reusable Starship, the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, is up and running.

Previous Booster 1095 missions GPS-III 8 | 6 Starlink missions USSF-432 was the 119th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, and the 14th national-security flight of the rocket so far this year. The vast majority of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 — more than 70% — have been devoted to building out the Starlink megaconstellation. SpaceX has also launched six other missions this year. Three were operational flights of the company's Falcon Heavy rocket, while the other three were test missions of its next-gen Starship vehicle. SpaceX plans to retire both the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy shortly after the fully reusable Starship, the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, is up and running.

item.title: 49ers rumors: Brandon Aiyuk’s reinstatement chances ‘not promising’ in 2026
item.description: Sep 27, 2020; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk (11) runs the ball against New York Giants defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence (97) during the first quarter of a NFL football game at MetLife Stadium. 49ers rumors: Brandon Aiyuk’s reinstatement chances ‘not promising’ in 2026 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers boast one of the most recognizable NFL rosters from a names perspective and wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, who spoke to media on Friday , November 6, is certainly one of them. Christian McCaffrey and Nick Bosa are expected to be back for Week 9 , while the 2023 Second Team All-Pro receiver Aiyuk has been working to be reinstated to the NFL after a high profile parting of ways with the 49ers. Aiyuk hasn’t played since the 2024-25 NFL season. He suffered a serious knee injury and missed team meetings leading to the voiding of about $27 million of his contract and Aiyuk’s subsequent public trolling of the 49ers franchise. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN chimed in on the situation as Aiyuk and agent Drew Rosenhaus spoke to media. Fowler is not bullish on Aiyuk’s chances of being reinstated this season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Aiyuk wants to get reinstated to play in the NFL. His prospects in the short term are not promising, assuming he becomes a free agent eventually,” Fowler said. The 49ers are moving forward with a Brock Purdy-led passing game that has been beset by injuries lately. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel aren’t expected to play against the Raiders in Week 9. Purdy commented on the Aiyuk situation recently , painting the picture of a team that likes what it has in the locker room right now with little plans of changing much. Aiyuk has a long way to go toward restoring goodwill in the NFL, even with a huge body of work behind him in the league. He is one of the better receivers the 49ers have seen in the last decade, but it appears as if his time with GM John Lynch’s team is coming to a close. Related: Brandon Aiyuk breaks silence before meeting with 49ers Related: 49ers’ Nick Bosa, Christian McCaffrey in, Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel out vs. Raiders

item.title: Old Tappan football dominates West Morris to reach sectional final
item.description: OLD TAPPAN - Zach Miceli completed his first 10 passes, and the Old Tappan senior did not throw his one and only incompletion until late in the third quarter. The Golden Knights scored on their first six possessions and rolled to a running-clock, 43-21 victory over West Morris on Nov. 6 in a North 1, Group 3 sectional football semifinal. Miceli threw for 244 yards and three touchdowns in three quarters to lead unbeaten Old Tappan, ranked No. 1 in the North Jersey Public Super 20 and No. 4 in the USA TODAY NETWORK New Jersey Super 25. Miceli threw first-half TDs of 60 and 50 yards to senior receiver Leo Etter and a 27-yard score to senior running back Nick Blanchard to help Old Tappan (10-0) build a 29-7 halftime lead. "We've got some guys who are dangerous kids in the pass game, and our quarterback is obviously who he is," Old Tappan coach Brian Dunn said of the three-year starter. Blanchard scored on third-quarter runs of 1 and 12 yards to extend the Golden Knights' lead to 43-7 and trigger the running clock. Run-heavy West Morris (7-4) scored its three TDs on the ground. Junior running back Deacon Frayne scored on a 9-yard run in the second quarter to trim the deficit to 15-7 Check back later for updates. This article originally appeared on NorthJersey.com: Old Tappan football dominates West Morris to reach sectional final

item.title: Knicks organization responds to Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride questioning Taylor Swift’s fandom
item.description: Knicks organization responds to Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride questioning Taylor Swift’s fandom originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Knicks have responded to Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride's recent comments about Taylor Swift that questioned her allegiance to the New York team. Kolek and McBride made an appearance on the NBA 2K League TikTok livestream this week when they were asked, “Who’s the fakest celeb fan you’ve seen courtside?” Kolek answered: “Maybe Taylor Swift?” McBride responded quickly, presuming how his teammate's response would unfold online, “I would agree…Swifties not gonna like that answer.” Kolek agreed with McBride's evaluation of his answer, “I’m gonna get some hate…I guess she’s got a lot going on…can’t come all the time…but it’s a little performative.” In the Knicks guard's defense, he did acknowledge that given her celebrity status, she has a super busy schedule and cannot attend games very often. Q “Who’s the fakest celeb fan you’ve seen courtside?” Tyler Kolek “Maybe Taylor Swift?” Deuce McBride “I would agree…Swifties not gonna like that answer” Kolek “I’m gonna get some hate…I guess she’s got a lot going on…can’t come all the time…but it’s a little performative” https://t.co/r7v4AJBK04 — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) November 5, 2026 What Did The Knicks Say In Response? The Knicks organization responded to Kolek and McBride's comments with a statement to Entertainment Weekly on Nov. 6. “Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization.” Swift's most recent appearance in Madison Square Garden to cheer on the team was for Game 4 of the NBA Finals when the Knicks faced the San Antonio Spurs. She sat courtside with friends Alana and Este Haim as well as Mariska Hargitay, where they all rocked custom shirts to cheer on the Knicks. The last time she was at MSG was ironically not basketball-related. She said "I do" to Travis Kelce on July 3 in front of 1,000 of their star-studded guests. Despite the comments that McBride and Kolek made questioning her Knicks fandom, the superstar has been sighted at home games since she moved to New York City in 2014. Kolek and McBride sharing their grievances on Swift's "performative" attendance follows their teammate Jose Alvarado expressing that he wants to see her at more games this season. "That's a surreal superstar, and I was happy she was cheering us on," the Knicks point guard told Us Weekly back in June. "And [she] seemed like she was having a good time, and we won, so even better." Alvarado told the outlet that, "She got to come more often." Kolek and McBride have not reacted to the Knicks' statement at this time. item.title: Ben James produces another low round and takes the 36-hole lead in Mexico
item.description: CABO SAN LUCAS, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 06: Ben James of the United States plays his shot from the fourth tee during the second round of the World Wide Technology Championship 2026 at El Cardonal at Diamante on November 06, 2026 in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images LOS CABOS, Mexico — Ben James ran off five straight birdies around the turn and finished with an aggressive tee shot for one last birdie and an 8-under 64 on Friday to build a one-shot lead going into the weekend at the World Wide Technology Championship. James, already assured his PGA Tour card for next year as the No. 1 player in the PGA Tour University ranking, had his 14th round of 65 or lower in 13 tournaments since turning pro out of Virginia this summer. He already has four finishes in the top 5 and picking up plenty of experience along the way. A victory would put him on the Championship Series under the new model in 2028 and move him into the top 50 in the world. “It’s weird, in college I was kind of someone that would shoot 2, 3 under every time out and would have trouble going low,” James said. “But you adapt to your surroundings as humans, so I guess out here that’s what you have to do. I’ve been rolling it well and playing well, so nice to be shooting some low numbers.” James was at 15-under 129 at the Tiger Woods-designed El Cardonal at Diamante. He was one shot ahead of Peter Malnati, who was tied for the lead until coming up short of the green on the par-3 ninth and missing a 12-foot par putt to end his round of 64. “I work really hard on my game and I haven’t had tons to show for that lately,” Malnati said. “So to not be in that position coming down the stretch on a Friday where ... I don’t even have to think about the cut line, I can think about playing golf. That was fun.” Zac Blair had a 68 and was three shots behind. This is the second time James has had the lead going into the weekend. The other was the RBC Canadian Open, and he shot a 78 to quickly spiral out of contention. He also had a good chance to win the Biltmore Championship Asheville until Jacob Bridgeman put on a putting clinic down the stretch in the final round. “I’m doing everything right,” James said. “But for me, I’m just trying to win each shot, just do the best I can for each golf shot and not thinking ahead and just do the best I can. And as I say, winning the shot at hand.” He won the par-5 18th when he least expected it. James has been relying on his short wedges, and hit a pedestrian pitch to about 18 feet. But he holed the putt, and then started the front nine with three straight birdies to set the target. This is among the last three tournaments of the FedEx Cup Fall, after which the top 100 players keep full status for next year.

item.title: Nick Saban Takes Subtle Shot at Marcus Freeman’s Notre Dame After Spotting Major Flaw Against BYU
item.description: September 5, 2026, Austin, Texas, USA: Former Alabama Crimson Tide Coach and ESPN College Gameday Analyst Nick Saban on the set. Austin USA – ZUMAl187 20260905_zsp_l187_027 Copyright: xJamesxLeyvax ©IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire Notre Dame has won seven of its first eight games, and its defense has given opponents very little room to work with. But the Fighting Irish still have one question to answer before the biggest game of their season: can their offense keep up when the competition gets tougher? Their loss to BYU brought that concern into focus, and with Miami coming to South Bend, the spotlight is now on Marcus Freeman’s team. The Irish are ranked No. 11 in the first College Football Playoff rankings and know that Saturday’s meeting with the No. 1 Hurricanes could shape their chances of making the field. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban has been watching the team closely, and one part of Notre Dame’s performance against BYU clearly stood out to him. “Notre Dame hasn’t been able to put it together in big games,” Saban said. “They got guys wide (expletive) open in the BYU game and hell, I can throw it to them. If a guy is open by 10 yards, you don’t have to make a perfect pass. Just get the ball to them,” Writer John Leuzzi posted on X on 7 November. Saban was pointing to the chances Notre Dame missed during its October 17 loss to BYU. The Irish went into halftime trailing 21-10 and never managed to turn things around. Quarterback CJ Carr completed 27 of 49 passes for 261 yards, finishing with a 55.1% completion rate and no passing touchdowns. Saban's critique reveals a critical weakness in Freeman's defensive scheme. Subscribe to stay ahead of college football's biggest coaching debates and strategic breakdowns. It was his lowest completion percentage of the season, and the missed throws became a concern heading into the Miami game. To be fair, Saban did have plenty of praise for Notre Dame. The Irish defense is allowing just 236.3 yards per game, the fewest in the country. It is also tied for fourth nationally in scoring defense, giving up 13.4 points per game. Notre Dame’s next game could make a major difference in its playoff hopes. At 7-1 and sitting at No. 11, the Irish have not yet picked up a win over a ranked opponent. With no other ranked teams remaining on their schedule after Miami, Saturday’s matchup gives them a chance to add the kind of win the selection committee wants to see. Saban made his feelings clear during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, calling the game a must-win for Freeman’s team. “This is a huge game. Obviously, playing the No. 1 team in the country at home. I think the game is kind of a must-win situation, because the College Football Playoff put them conveniently at No. 11. ‘Conveniently’ means if they don’t win, they may be on the outside looking in. Not saying they can’t play their way back into it, but they don’t have the strongest schedule to finish with.” Saban also made sure to point out that he likes Not

Austin USA – ZUMAl187 20260905_zsp_l187_027 Copyright: xJamesxLeyvax ©IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire Notre Dame has won seven of its first eight games, and its defense has given opponents very little room to work with. But the Fighting Irish still have one question to answer before the biggest game of their season: can their offense keep up when the competition gets tougher? Their loss to BYU brought that concern into focus, and with Miami coming to South Bend, the spotlight is now on Marcus Freeman’s team. The Irish are ranked No. 11 in the first College Football Playoff rankings and know that Saturday’s meeting with the No. 1 Hurricanes could shape their chances of making the field. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban has been watching the team closely, and one part of Notre Dame’s performance against BYU clearly stood out to him. “Notre Dame hasn’t been able to put it together in big games,” Saban said. “They got guys wide (expletive) open in the BYU game and hell, I can throw it to them. If a guy is open by 10 yards, you don’t have to make a perfect pass. Just get the ball to them,” Writer John Leuzzi posted on X on 7 November. Saban was pointing to the chances Notre Dame missed during its October 17 loss to BYU. The Irish went into halftime trailing 21-10 and never managed to turn things around. Quarterback CJ Carr completed 27 of 49 passes for 261 yards, finishing with a 55.1% completion rate and no passing touchdowns. Saban's critique reveals a critical weakness in Freeman's defensive scheme. Subscribe to stay ahead of college football's biggest coaching debates and strategic breakdowns. It was his lowest completion percentage of the season, and the missed throws became a concern heading into the Miami game. To be fair, Saban did have plenty of praise for Notre Dame. The Irish defense is allowing just 236.3 yards per game, the fewest in the country. It is also tied for fourth nationally in scoring defense, giving up 13.4 points per game. Notre Dame’s next game could make a major difference in its playoff hopes. At 7-1 and sitting at No. 11, the Irish have not yet picked up a win over a ranked opponent. With no other ranked teams remaining on their schedule after Miami, Saturday’s matchup gives them a chance to add the kind of win the selection committee wants to see. Saban made his feelings clear during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, calling the game a must-win for Freeman’s team. “This is a huge game. Obviously, playing the No. 1 team in the country at home. I think the game is kind of a must-win situation, because the College Football Playoff put them conveniently at No. 11. ‘Conveniently’ means if they don’t win, they may be on the outside looking in. Not saying they can’t play their way back into it, but they don’t have the strongest schedule to finish with.” Saban also made sure to point out that he likes Notre Dame’s defense and Freeman’s approach. Still, he believes the Irish need a quality win to strengthen their playoff case. Miami enters the game as the No. 1 team in the CFP rankings. The Hurricanes are also expected to be without star wide receiver Malachi Toney, who is dealing with an ankle injury that will require a medical procedure and keep him out for an extended period. Notre Dame was not the only topic Saban discussed during his appearance on the New Heights podcast with Jason and Travis Kelce. He also spoke about the planned expansion of the College Football Playoff from 12 teams to 24, which is expected to begin in 2027. “There’s not 24 teams in the country that can win the National Championship,” Saban said. He questioned why college football needs such a large playoff field and suggested that money is a major reason behind the proposed change. “Playing in the SEC Championship was a big thing to our players, it was a big thing to our fans, it was a tradition, and it was a great venue,” he said. “There’s a lot of pride in winning the conference championship. And we’re going to give that up to have an extra game, where the 24th team is going to play the ninth-best team. I’m not a big (proponent) of it.” Saban also questioned whether the additional playoff round would bring in enough money to make up for the revenue lost from conference championship games. While he has suggested that a 16-team format could be a middle ground, he is not convinced that 24 teams are needed. For now, Notre Dame has a more immediate challenge to deal with. Freeman’s team has the defense to compete with the country’s top programs, but the game against Miami will give its offense a chance to show it can deliver when the pressure is on. A win would give the Irish the signature result they have been missing. A loss could leave their playoff hopes in a much tougher position. item.title: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Makes Decisive Statement on NFL Trade Deadline
item.description: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Selling? No, the Dallas Cowboys will not be selling at the NFL trade deadline, which looms in just four days. The team must play a game–a pretty important game, really, as all these games are now made much more important thanks to recent failures–against the Colts on the road and, in doing so, they will see what a team in the midst of a massive sell looks like. The Colts have dumped stars in the past 10 days, and could dump at least one more if running back Jonathan Taylor is sent out by Tuesday. Might playing against a team in the throws of an on-the-fly rebuild inspire team owner Jerry Jones to shift his thinking and rebuild his spent draft capital? There has been ample conversation about trading away George Pickens, but that has apparently been more smoke than fire. But whether things could change was the question put to Jones on Friday afternoon during a radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, and the owner was clear in his stance. Cowboys ‘Commitment’ Won’t Change at NFL Trade Deadline Jones still thinks the 2026 Cowboys can be a good team. It’s an absurd thought based on the results so far, but maybe not so absurd when you consider the talent level on this team and the fact that the Cowboys are 3-5 and somehow still in a good position to win their otherwise terrible division. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tells @OThankKevin, @inthemageors and @AlecOnTheRadio that he's "a lot more likely" to add to the roster than sell at the trade deadline pic.twitter.com/eSshzPaZ9S— 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) November 6, 2026 Jones made that clear with his answer: “I have, I really believe that we have a team that the work we have done over the last 18 months, last year and this year, has real potential to play better than it’s played now. My situation, and I am not talking about Indianapolis, I am not talking about any other team, our situation, because the amount and the commitment and the changes we have made, it’s not the smart thing to do to make big adjustments. I would much more likely be adding to this direction than taking away from it.” The Cowboys will play the Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Indianapolis. The NFL trade deadline follows on Tuesday, November 10. item.content:encoded: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Selling? No, the Dallas Cowboys will not be selling at the NFL trade deadline, which looms in just four days. The team must play a game–a pretty important game, really, as all these games are now made much more important thanks to recent failures–against the Colts on the road and, in doing so, they will see what a team in the midst of a massive sell looks like. The Colts have dumped stars in the past 10 days, and could dump at least one more if running back Jonathan Taylor is sent out by Tuesday. Might playing against a team in the throws of an on-the-fly rebuild inspire team owner Jerry Jones to shift his thinking and rebuild his spent draft capital? There has been ample conversation about trading away George Pickens, but that has apparently been more smoke than fire. But whether things could change was the question put to Jones on Friday afternoon during a radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, and the owner was clear in his stance. Cowboys ‘Commitment’ Won’t Change at NFL Trade Deadline Jones still thinks the 2026 Cowboys can be a good team. It’s an absurd thought based on the results so far, but maybe not so absurd when you consider the talent level on this team and the fact that the Cowboys are 3-5 and somehow still in a good position to win their otherwise terrible division. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tells @OThankKevin, @inthemageors and @AlecOnTheRadio that he's "a lot more likely" to add to the roster than sell at the trade deadline pic.twitter.com/eSshzPaZ9S— 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) November 6, 2026 Jones made that clear with his answer: “I have, I really believe that we have a team that the work we have done over the last 18 months, last year and this year, has real potential to play better than it’s played now. My situation, and I am not talking about Indianapolis, I am not talking about any other team, our situation, because the amount and the commitment and the changes we have made, it’s not the smart thing to do to make big adjustments. I would much more likely be adding to this direction than taking away from it.” The Cowboys will play the Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Indianapolis. The NFL trade deadline follows on Tuesday, November 10. item.title: NASCAR’s Denny Hamlin Sends Blunt Message on Chances at First Championship
item.description: Denny Hamlin delivers a blunt assessment of his chances to win his first NASCAR Cup Series championship ahead of the season finale at Homestead-Miami. Getty Denny Hamlin enters Sunday’s NASCAR Cup Series finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway 70 points behind Kyle Larson and sees no realistic way to erase the gap. In fact, speaking at a press availability on Friday, Hamlin compared his chances to catch Larson and bring home the Cup to winning the lottery. “I mean, I don’t have any optimism. There’s obviously a chance you can win the lottery as well,” he said, sending a blunt message on where he believes he stands, as quoted by reporter Jeff Gluck. Hamlin has won 64 Cup races, more than all but eight drivers in NASCAR history. Yet somehow, he has never won a championship. His ‘don’t have any optimism’ remark followed Hamlin’s sixth-place finish at Martinsville Speedway on Nov. 1, where he called the title “unrealistic for sure,” as quoted by NASCAR.com after the race. He said the deficit to Larson needed to sit in the 40s to leave the No. 11 team with any degree of viable hope. Read More From Heavy NASCAR’s Kyle Larson Makes Surprising Admission Ahead of Championship Race Hamlin Faces Long Odds at Homestead-Miami Speedway Larson leads the standings, with Christopher Bell 67 points back and Hamlin third, 70 behind. Larson needs only nine points at Homestead to clinch the title no matter what his rivals do, and a 28th-place finish would be enough to get it done, even if he scores no stage points. Hamlin’s route is far narrower. He must both win the race and collect 17 of the 20 available stage points, or 16 if he also takes the fastest-lap point, according to calculations by Fox Sports insider Bob Pockrass . Larson would also need to finish 29th or worse without a stage point. The most any driver can collect is 76 points in a perfect race . Hamlin won the regular-season title and started Martinsville from the pole, but he trimmed the gap by only three points . A decision not to pit during Stage 1 left Hamlin 17th at the end of the segment, while Larson ran 23rd, one lap down, and neither driver scored a stage point all day. “We just didn’t gain enough to make it realistic,” Hamlin said, according to Pockrass. Hamlin has won 64 Cup races, more than all but eight drivers in NASCAR history. Yet somehow, he has never won a championship. His ‘don’t have any optimism’ remark followed Hamlin’s sixth-place finish at Martinsville Speedway on Nov. 1, where he called the title “unrealistic for sure,” as quoted by NASCAR.com after the race. He said the deficit to Larson needed to sit in the 40s to leave the No. 11 team with any degree of viable hope. Read More From Heavy NASCAR’s Kyle Larson Makes Surprising Admission Ahead of Championship Race Hamlin Faces Long Odds at Homestead-Miami Speedway Larson leads the standings, with Christopher Bell 67 points back and Hamlin third, 70 behind. Larson needs only nine points at Homestead to clinch the title no matter what his rivals do, and a 28th-place finish would be enough to get it done, even if he scores no stage points. Hamlin’s route is far narrower. He must both win the race and collect 17 of the 20 available stage points, or 16 if he also takes the fastest-lap point, according to calculations by Fox Sports insider Bob Pockrass . Larson would also need to finish 29th or worse without a stage point. The most any driver can collect is 76 points in a perfect race . Hamlin won the regular-season title and started Martinsville from the pole, but he trimmed the gap by only three points . Read More From Heavy NASCAR CEO Gives Surprising Carson Hocevar Verdict Before Championship Race Denny Hamlin’s Powerball Win and Career Résumé Hamlin has cashed a lottery ticket before. During a 2022 race weekend in Phoenix, he says that he bought $300 worth of Powerball tickets at a Scottsdale gas station and matched five of six numbers , including the Powerball, for a $50,000 prize. The odds of winning that prize stand at 1 in 913,130 . Hamlin collected again in Las Vegas in March 2025, where a $300 bet on a Buffalo slot machine paid $126,150 on a single spin and two nights of play totaled more than $200,000. His lottery comparison therefore comes from experience. Hamlin has cashed a Powerball ticket and a Las Vegas jackpot, but not a Powerball grand prize or a Cup championship. Hamlin was born Nov. 18, 1980, in Tampa , Florida, and raised in Chesterfield, Virginia. He signed with Joe Gibbs Racing in 2004 and won at Pocono on June 11, 2006 , the first of his 64 Cup victories. Eight of those wins have come at Pocono, where he swept both races that first season. He owns three Daytona 500 victories, in 2016, 2019 and 2020, and co-owns 23XI Racing with NBA legend Michael Jordan . He finished second in the standings in 2010, when he led Jimmie Johnson by 15 points entering the finale, and again in 2025, when he led 208 laps at Phoenix Raceway but finished sixth after a late caution forced overtime. Hamlin has said 2027 will be his final season in the Cup Series. He turns 46 on Nov. 18 and is the oldest full-time driver in the series, according to The Associated Press. His father, who was terminally ill, died in a house fire during the offseason, according to Fox Sports. Larson, the 2025 champion, would claim his third Cup title by clinching Sunday. item.title: Klay Thompson Admits He Still Thinks About Returning To Warriors
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Not too long ago, Klay Thompson was enjoying historic prosperity on the Golden State Warriors . Alongside Stephen Curry , Draymond Green , and (for some years) Kevin Durant , he helped usher in an era of dominance for the franchise that no basketball fan will soon forget. Now that it’s over, however, we can only look back and reflect on what was. For Klay, who is on the Miami Heat now, so much has changed in a relatively short time. Yesterday, against his former team, he was reminded of that fact, and his response tells us a lot about how he thinks of his time there. According to Klay, he still thinks about his Warriors run and potentially going back there, where it all began. “A little bit,” said Klay after the game . “And I’m so grateful for the support I have in the region. I mean, just going to breakfast this morning and seeing familiar faces. It was awesome. And I’m very, very grateful for the fandom. It really inspires me to keep going.” Of course, Thompson has been out of San Francisco for years now, but it’s always a weird experience facing Steph. They once won championships together, and now Klay gets assigned to guard him, just like the opponents they used to beat. Unfortunately for the NBA veteran, Curry got the better of him last night, with a final stat line of 29 points, one rebound, four assists, and one steal on 47.4% shooting from the field. “It was fun. It was really fun,” Thompson said on the matchup with Curry . “Steph’s super crafty still to this day, and felt good to block his shot. He made a great up-and-under on me. He had an incredible night, and you know what Steph’s doing. I mean, I might not have appreciated it as much as his teammate, ‘cause I got to see it every night, so it became normal. But to see it as an opponent, it’s incredible. Especially that he’s nearing 40 and he moves like a young man, like a young athlete. It’s just all the respect in the world for him. He deserves all the accolades, the adulation, the money, and he’s just one of one, and the game’s going to miss him when he does hang it up.” Klay left the Dubs to pursue a championship on his own terms , but it hasn’t panned out as he hoped. After a failed stint with the Dallas Mavericks , he signed with the Heat this summer, only for them to start 3-6. Meanwhile, the Warriors are moving in a positive direction after securing six straight wins . Even Thompson has no choice but to acknowledge their talent. “The Dubs are very good,” Thompson added . “I mean, they have a system in place that has been successful since Steve became the head coach, and never count out the Dubs, especially with Steph and Draymond out there. I mean, Jimmy coming back, Moses coming back. So, strength in numbers has always been their mantra. According to Klay, he still thinks about his Warriors run and potentially going back there, where it all began. “A little bit,” said Klay after the game . “And I’m so grateful for the support I have in the region. Unfortunately for the NBA veteran, Curry got the better of him last night, with a final stat line of 29 points, one rebound, four assists, and one steal on 47.4% shooting from the field. “It was fun. It was really fun,” Thompson said on the matchup with Curry . “Steph’s super crafty still to this day, and felt good to block his shot. He made a great up-and-under on me. He had an incredible night, and you know what Steph’s doing. I mean, I might not have appreciated it as much as his teammate, ‘cause I got to see it every night, so it became normal. But to see it as an opponent, it’s incredible. Especially that he’s nearing 40 and he moves like a young man, like a young athlete. It’s just all the respect in the world for him. He deserves all the accolades, the adulation, the money, and he’s just one of one, and the game’s going to miss him when he does hang it up.” Klay left the Dubs to pursue a championship on his own terms , but it hasn’t panned out as he hoped. I mean, Jimmy coming back, Moses coming back. So, strength in numbers has always been their mantra. And I think they’ll be a force in the West.” At 36, it’s not too late for Klay Thompson to reunite with his former team. With a $5.8 million player option next summer, he could opt out and become a free agent in 2027, setting a clear pathway for him to re-join Steph and Draymond. Plus, with Yaxel Lendeborg and Jimmy Butler , there would be a real chance to make another title run. Until then, the best Klay can do is reflect on the past and celebrate what he was able to accomplish. As a four-time champion, five-time All-Star, and two-time All-NBA player, his legacy has already been set as an all-time great, and nothing he does going forward will top the heights he reached during his prime.

item.title: By the numbers: Ohio State ices out Youngstown State, 89-65
item.description: COLUMBUS, OH - OCTOBER 25: Ohio State Buckeyes guard Justin Pippen (10) and Ohio State Buckeyes forward Andrija Jelavic (4) walk down the court during the men's college exhibition basketball game between the Butler Bulldogs and Ohio State Buckeyes on October 25, 2026, at The Schottenstein Center in Columbus, OH. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Alexa, play “Back In the Saddle” by Aerosmith. For the first time in eight months, Ohio State was back in the Schottenstein Center on Friday night, taking on in-state foe Youngstown State in Ohio State’s home opener. The Buckeyes came into this game 6-0 against the Penguins all-time, with the most recent win coming on November 11, 2024. John Mobley Jr. and Aaron Bradshaw each scored 16 points in Ohio State’s 81-47 win. The aforementioned Mobley made his 55th start in an Ohio State uniform, alongside Justin Pippen, Anthony Thompson, Amare Bynum, and Andrija Jelavic. Despite Ohio State’s obvious advantage in this game both on paper this season and in the all-time series between the two, Jake Diebler said on Thursday afternoon that the Buckeyes would need to be hyper-aware of YSU’s guards on the perimeter, especially junior guard Linus Holmstrom. The 6-foot-3 Swedish guard scored 26 points in Youngstown State’s season-opening 79-71 win over St. Bonaventure on Monday night, including going 6-for-13 from beyond the arc. Holmstrom was a 39.4% three-point shooter last season. The aforementioned Holmstrom made an early impact on the game Friday night, knocking down three-pointers on back-to-back possessions 15 seconds apart to give the Penguins a 10-8 lead with 15:17 left in the first half. Ohio State struggled to shake off the Penguins in the first half, retaking a 21-19 lead on a second-chance bucket by Andrija Jelavic with 8:54 remaining in the opening stanza. The Buckeyes were mauling Youngstown State on the glass, but their first eight offensive rebounds led to just two second-chance points somehow. Ohio State was reading the ball off the rim and beating the Penguins to the glass, but were failing to convert on a bunch of high-percentage looks around the basket. Jake Diebler called timeout, and immediately out of that timeout Justin Pippen threw the ball to nobody along the baseline for a turnover, and then Amare Bynum fouled Coleman shooting a three-pointer just in front of the Ohio State bench. Coleman hit just one of the three, putting Youngstown State up 31-28 with just over three minutes left in the first half. item.content:encoded: COLUMBUS, OH - OCTOBER 25: Ohio State Buckeyes guard Justin Pippen (10) and Ohio State Buckeyes forward Andrija Jelavic (4) walk down the court during the men's college exhibition basketball game between the Butler Bulldogs and Ohio State Buckeyes on October 25, 2026, at The Schottenstein Center in Columbus, OH. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Alexa, play “Back In the Saddle” by Aerosmith. For the first time in eight months, Ohio State was back in the Schottenstein Center on Friday night, taking on in-state foe Youngstown State in Ohio State’s home opener. The Buckeyes came into this game 6-0 against the Penguins all-time, with the most recent win coming on November 11, 2024. John Mobley Jr. and Aaron Bradshaw each scored 16 points in Ohio State’s 81-47 win. The aforementioned Mobley made his 55th start in an Ohio State uniform, alongside Justin Pippen, Anthony Thompson, Amare Bynum, and Andrija Jelavic. Despite Ohio State’s obvious advantage in this game both on paper this season and in the all-time series between the two, Jake Diebler said on Thursday afternoon that the Buckeyes would need to be hyper-aware of YSU’s guards on the perimeter, especially junior guard Linus Holmstrom. The 6-foot-3 Swedish guard scored 26 points in Youngstown State’s season-opening 79-71 win over St. Bonaventure on Monday night, including going 6-for-13 from beyond the arc. Holmstrom was a 39.4% three-point shooter last season. The aforementioned Holmstrom made an early impact on the game Friday night, knocking down three-pointers on back-to-back possessions 15 seconds apart to give the Penguins a 10-8 lead with 15:17 left in the first half. Ohio State struggled to shake off the Penguins in the first half, retaking a 21-19 lead on a second-chance bucket by Andrija Jelavic with 8:54 remaining in the opening stanza. The Buckeyes were mauling Youngstown State on the glass, but their first eight offensive rebounds led to just two second-chance points somehow. Ohio State was reading the ball off the rim and beating the Penguins to the glass, but were failing to convert on a bunch of high-percentage looks around the basket. Buckeyes get it done on both ends 💥 @OhioStateHoops Subscribe/watch on B1G+ https://t.co/pgjoeDWOus pic.twitter.com/bAtizOQ0SC — Big Ten Men's Basketball (@B1GMBBall) November 6, 2026 Back-to-back three-pointers for Youngstown State’s Jermaine Coleman put the Penguins back in front, 30-28, with 3:52 remaining in the first half. Jake Diebler called timeout, and immediately out of that timeout Justin Pippen threw the ball to nobody along the baseline for a turnover, and then Amare Bynum fouled Coleman shooting a three-pointer just in front of the Ohio State bench. Coleman hit just one of the three, putting Youngstown State up 31-28 with just over three minutes left in the first half. Ohio State ripped off a 10-2 run to end the first half, taking a 38-33 lead into the locker room. Mobley scored four and Pippen connected for Ohio State’s first three-pointer of the game with 1:36 to go until the halftime break. The scored stayed within three points in either direction for the first 10 minutes of the second half, with Youngstown State taking the lead multiple times, only for Ohio State to come back moments later. With Ohio State up 55-52 and just under 10 minutes left in the game, Jelavic knocked down a three and dropped in a layup on back-to-back possessions to give Ohio State a 60-52 lead — its biggest margin of the night to that point. Those two buckets put Jelavic at 15 points on the night — a new career-high for the junior from Croatia. That's 20 points and counting for Juni 🎯 📺 Subscribe/watch on B1G+ https://t.co/yw0nKRa1a4 pic.twitter.com/kmR41HdWZ4 — Ohio State Hoops (@OhioStateHoops) November 7, 2026 Despite the lid never really coming off the basket from long range at any point, Ohio State was able to separate from Youngstown State over the final 10 minutes, and pulled away for a 89-65 victory at home. John Mobley Jr. recorded his 16th career 20-point game, finishing with 25 on 7-for-9 shooting. Jelavic finished with a career-high 21 points to go along with nine rebounds. Ohio State picked up its first win of the season Friday night. Here are a few key numbers and statistics from the Buckeyes’ victory: 1: Dunk (and technical) for John Mobley Jr. With just over 10 minutes remaining in the first half, Mobley stole the ball from Coleman near the free throw line and took off the other way like a wide receiver in broken coverage. Mobley, who is generously listed at 6-foot-2 on the Ohio State roster, had never dunked in-game before. With nobody in front of him, he rose up and threw down a two-handed jam, putting Ohio State ahead 19-16. However, the nearest official determined that Mobley had hung on the rim for a second too long, and assessed the junior a technical foul on his first career dunk. Diebler was incensed, but Youngstown State hit the automatic free throw to get the score back to 19-17 with 10:11 remaining in the first half. 1: First-half three-pointer for Ohio State Part of the reason Ohio State couldn’t shake free of Youngstown State in the first half was their complete inability to knock down a three-pointer. Not a single Buckeye was able to connect from deep until Pippen hit one from the left wing, just in front of the Youngstown State bench with 1:36 remaining in the first half that gave Ohio State a 36-31 lead. 12: First-half offensive rebounds for Ohio State Last season, Ohio State averaged 9.2 offensive rebounds per game. On Friday night, the Buckeyes had 12 in the first half alone, giving them additional opportunities to score and put some distance between themselves and Youngstown State. Unfortunately, that didn’t result in much, as those 12 offensive rebounds turned into just six second-chance points as Ohio State struggled mightily to get the lid off the basket. Still, when the coaching staff reviews the film from Friday night’s game, they’ll like to see that Ohio State was creating those second-chance opportunities that they didn’t create very often last season. 13: Consecutive points for Ohio State to pull away The game was nip and tuck for the better part of 30 minutes, and the possibility of Ohio State losing to Youngstown State for the first time ever hung in the air for all 8,000 or so nervous fans. But with 10:20 remaining in the game, Ohio State ripped off a 13-0 run that put them ahead 66-52 and all but sealed this one for the home team. Jelavic was a catalyst during the run, scoring seven of Ohio State’s 13 as he marched toward an eventual career-night. 21: Points for Andrija Jelavic – a career-high 5️⃣ straight points from Jelavic 🗣️ 📺 B1G+ | #GoBucks pic.twitter.com/7Ir1YbL7oZ — Ohio State Hoops (@OhioStateHoops) November 7, 2026 The 6-foot-11 transfer from Kentucky notched a career-high in scoring on Friday night, continuing his strong start to the season with 21 points on 10-for-16 shooting. He knocked down a three-pointer for the second consecutive game as well, and seems to have a stranglehold on the starting center spot for Ohio State for now.

item.title: Ryan Gosling is Officially Reviving The Flintstones for New Project
item.description: Ryan Gosling has been incredibly booked and busy of late. He starred in the lead role in the sci-fi smash hit Project Hail Mary earlier this year. In 2027, he'll travel to the galaxy far, far away in St ar Wars: Starfighter . Then in 2028 he'll make his long-awaited MCU debut as Ghost Rider , re-teaming with Starfighter director Shawn Levy. If all that wasn't enough, Gosling has lined up one more unexpected project: The Flintstones .

item.title: ‘I’m The Real Champion’
item.description: NEWARK, NEW JERSEY - MAY 09: Khamzat Chimaev of Russia prepares to face Sean Strickland in the UFC middleweight championship fight during the UFC 328 event at Prudential Center on May 09, 2026 in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC) Khamzat Chimaev wants his UFC middleweight championship back and he’s willing to wait on the sidelines to get it. It’s been nearly six months since Chimaev suffered a massive upset loss at the hands of Sean Strickland at UFC 328, but the wound is still fresh. That’s because Chimaev was expected to handle Strickland in dominant fashion and start a 185-pound title reign that we haven’t seen since Israel Adesanya. Unfortunately for Chimaev, Strickland stifled his grappling efforts and ended up winning a decision to walk away with the undisputed UFC middleweight crown. Chimaev, who has been staying busy under the Real American Freestyle (RAF) banner , is steadfast on getting his title back and revenge on Strickland. The previously undefeated champion even stated that he’d follow Strickland all the way up to heavyweight in order to get a rematch. Some believe Chimaev had a bad training camp and weight cut for the first fight and that he’d right that wrong in another matchup with Strickland. The only problem is that Chimaev isn’t directly in line for another title shot. That belongs to red-hot contender Nassourdine Imavov, who is expected to fight Strickland in early 2027 if all things play out. Until then, Chimaev can only lobby for another shot at UFC’s 185-pound title and that’s exactly what he’s doing. The middleweight contender is willing to wait to fight the winner of Strickland and Imavov no matter how long it takes. It wouldn’t be a huge stretch for Chimaev heading into next year considering he hasn’t fought twice in one year since 2022. “I should fight the winner [of Strickland vs Imavov] because I’m the #1 contender,” said Chimaev in a recent interview with MMA Junkie . “I didn’t lose that match. I’m the real champion.”

item.title: 49ers' ‘Hulk' was a zero-star recruit. Now he's manhandling NFL linemen
item.description: San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle Sebastian Valdez reacts following an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, in Seattle. (AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson) (Lindsey Wasson/Associated Press) In 2021, an 18-year-old Sebastian Valdez traversed up I-15 North to depart his hometown of Spring Valley for a much less familiar place called Bozeman, Montana. Uncertainty hung in the air. He was set to begin his freshman season at Montana State with a new head coach, a new defensive coordinator and a new position coach - none of whom recruited him to the school. Shawn Howe, the Bobcats' first-year defensive line coach, scanned his new group of players at one of the team's first organized practices. Among them, a scrawny, zero-star freshman edge rusher immediately popped. It was Valdez. Right then and there, Howe forecasted the young man's future. "That's the next 3-technique (defensive tackle) at Montana State," Howe, now a defensive assistant with the Pittsburgh Steelers, recalled thinking. Even if Valdez didn't know it at the time, Howe was right. And even though Howe was right, the moment came a little sooner than either of them could have envisioned. During the first week of the season, one of Montana State's starting defensive tackles blew out his knee. That's when Howe called Valdez into his office. "Hey, we're gonna move you to D-tackle," he said, "and you're the future of this position." In that moment, Valdez recalled, anxiety bubbled. He had a lot of questions. But he wasn't going to turn back now. "He just laid out this whole vision for me, and I just trusted him," Valdez told the Chronicle on Thursday. "And yeah, the rest is history." San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle Sebastian Valdez (55) delivers a hit on Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels on Oct. 19 in Santa Clara. (Jed Jacobsohn/Associated Press) Five years after being thrust into the spotlight at a Football Championship Subdivision school, Valdez, a 2025 undrafted free agent, is a 6-foot-3, 301-pound rotation regular for the San Francisco 49ers . The 24-year-old defensive tackle earned his first standard NFL contract last month after spending more than a year toiling on the 49ers' practice squad. In five career games, he has recorded nine tackles, three quarterback hits, two tackles-for-loss and a sack. And most importantly, he looks like he belongs. What have Valdez's teammates, who dubbed him "The Hulk" because of his immense strength, thought of his play so far? One teammate offered a three-word response. "Manhandling dudes, bro," fellow defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa said. ‘They didn't understand' In a league full of underdog stories, Valdez owns one of extreme proportions. Unlike most NFL players, Valdez never dreamed of this life as a kid. He didn't play football until sixth grade. item.content:encoded: San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle Sebastian Valdez reacts following an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, in Seattle. (AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson) (Lindsey Wasson/Associated Press) In 2021, an 18-year-old Sebastian Valdez traversed up I-15 North to depart his hometown of Spring Valley for a much less familiar place called Bozeman, Montana. Uncertainty hung in the air. He was set to begin his freshman season at Montana State with a new head coach, a new defensive coordinator and a new position coach - none of whom recruited him to the school. Shawn Howe, the Bobcats' first-year defensive line coach, scanned his new group of players at one of the team's first organized practices. Among them, a scrawny, zero-star freshman edge rusher immediately popped. It was Valdez. Right then and there, Howe forecasted the young man's future. "That's the next 3-technique (defensive tackle) at Montana State," Howe, now a defensive assistant with the Pittsburgh Steelers, recalled thinking. Even if Valdez didn't know it at the time, Howe was right. And even though Howe was right, the moment came a little sooner than either of them could have envisioned. During the first week of the season, one of Montana State's starting defensive tackles blew out his knee. That's when Howe called Valdez into his office. "Hey, we're gonna move you to D-tackle," he said, "and you're the future of this position." In that moment, Valdez recalled, anxiety bubbled. He had a lot of questions. But he wasn't going to turn back now. "He just laid out this whole vision for me, and I just trusted him," Valdez told the Chronicle on Thursday. "And yeah, the rest is history." San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle Sebastian Valdez (55) delivers a hit on Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels on Oct. 19 in Santa Clara. (Jed Jacobsohn/Associated Press) Five years after being thrust into the spotlight at a Football Championship Subdivision school, Valdez, a 2025 undrafted free agent, is a 6-foot-3, 301-pound rotation regular for the San Francisco 49ers . The 24-year-old defensive tackle earned his first standard NFL contract last month after spending more than a year toiling on the 49ers' practice squad. In five career games, he has recorded nine tackles, three quarterback hits, two tackles-for-loss and a sack. And most importantly, he looks like he belongs. What have Valdez's teammates, who dubbed him "The Hulk" because of his immense strength, thought of his play so far? One teammate offered a three-word response. "Manhandling dudes, bro," fellow defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa said. ‘They didn't understand' In a league full of underdog stories, Valdez owns one of extreme proportions. Unlike most NFL players, Valdez never dreamed of this life as a kid. He didn't play football until sixth grade. He was a no-star recruit out of Monte Vista High School in Southern California, where he also wrestled for three years and won a CIF state championship. In fact, Valdez said, "there was a point in high school that I enjoyed wrestling more than football." Despite his success on the mat, he earned no collegiate wrestling offers. He did receive one in football, though, so he informed his parents - both Mexican immigrants - of his intentions to attend Montana State on a scholarship. Jesús and Norah Valdez struggled to grasp the concept. "My parents never even, like - they didn't even understand how football works," Valdez said. "They didn't understand that I was gonna go away for school and that it was free." They eventually understood, and Valdez went off to Bozeman for his freshman campaign under a new and unfamiliar coaching staff. He played "pretty solid" as a fill-in defensive tackle as a freshman, he said, yet there was one problem. In order to play defensive tackle, he needed to add weight. And a lot of it. Howe instructed Valdez, weighing around 235 pounds at the time, to eat like crazy, but in a controlled manner. "He didn't want me getting, like, fat," Valdez deadpanned. So, what did he eat to remain in an extreme caloric surplus as a college student living in the middle of Montana? "Oh, man," Valdez said with a chuckle. "It was chicken and rice, chicken and rice. I can't even eat chicken and rice anymore. … It was just constantly that. "Even my roommates would see me with a little scale to weigh food, and they were kind of like, ‘What are you doing? ' And I was just like, ‘Man, trust. Like, I got to do this.' And it worked out. Gained the weight the right way. My speed, my strength got better … I think my second year I was like 265 (pounds)." Gracen Halton, middle, celebrates with Sebastian Valdez (55) and Khalid Kareem (47) after the 49ers sacked Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels on Oct. 19. (Jed Jacobsohn/Associated Press) Valdez spent three seasons in Bozeman. He played his senior campaign at the University of Washington, which offered a steep increase in competition. Valdez didn't exactly produce: two sacks and 4½ tackles for loss in 13 games. But he spent the better part of that year playing through an elbow injury that forced him to "walk on eggshells," according to Jason Kaufusi, Washington's defensive line coach, and damaged his draft stock. Valdez failed to earn a 2025 draft combine invite. Instead, his freakish athletic traits popped at the Huskies' on-campus pro day. Niners guard Carver Willis, who had just transferred from Kansas State to Washington, attended the event. He recalled being in awe while watching Valdez bench press 225 pounds 34 times (which would have led all players at the combine) and run the 40-yard dash in under 5 seconds. "He basically looked like the UW Hulk," Willis said. "I was like, ‘Oh, this guy's a dude .'" Still, Valdez went undrafted. He signed with the 49ers - largely because of how he fit into their scheme - as a free agent. As a rookie, he sat idly on the 49ers' practice squad. Head coach Kyle Shanahan elevated him to the active roster for multiple games last season, not with the intention to play him but rather as a "reward" for his hard work. At that point, San Francisco almost lost Valdez to the Steelers, who wanted to sign him off San Francisco's practice squad. But Valdez opted against it, explaining that "the vision that the 49ers had for me - and I think the vision I had for myself with this team - was a lot greater than what I had with the Steelers." He added that Pittsburgh's' "read attack" system doesn't suit him as well. Said Shanahan: "He was someone we really gambled with. It was someone we were very nervous about losing. We feel lucky that we didn't because he was playing at that level" while on the practice squad. ‘I gotta work for everything' In 2026, after a strong preseason, Valdez again didn't make the cut for the 53-man roster. Sensing a theme here? Earning football respect has never come easy for Valdez. "It's been like that every year with me," he said. "I gotta work for everything I have in my life. It's not a surprise to me." Was he beginning to doubt himself? He claims not. "It was only a matter of time," Valdez said, "whether it was here or somewhere else. I didn't want to go into a hole mentally. I just wanted to stay true to myself and still come in, have a routine and practice the way I practice, and I knew things would work out eventually." Odighizuwa shared a similar message with the second-year player at that point: "I'm like, ‘Don't stop working. I know you're not going to, but like, especially with how things are going around here (with the injuries). … Your opportunity is right around the corner.'" Odighizuwa was right. After nearly every defensive tackle ahead of him got hurt, Valdez got his chance. He impressed enough in San Francisco's Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals to earn a spot on the active roster. And on Oct. 11 against the Seattle Seahawks, Valdez had his moment. Sebastian Valdez signs autographs before a game in Seattle on Oct. 11. (Lind

item.title: Kentucky vs. Tennessee Injury Report: Sam Greene remains probable
item.description: The final injury report is out for the Kentucky Wildcats and the Tennessee Volunteers as they prepare for their Saturday showdown at Neyland Stadium. For Kentucky, star edge rusher Sam Greene remains listed as probable, so he continues to trend toward playing Saturday night. That would be a major boost for Kentucky’s defense, which struggled at home in the win over Vanderbilt when Greene was out of the lineup. Backup cornerback Isaiah McMillian remains probable, so he should play following his injury scare in that win over the Commodores. Finally, linebacker Antwan Smith, cornerback Jaden Smith, linebacker Justyn Hartley, and cornerback Grant Grayton remain listed as out. And for Tennessee, their injury report also stayed the same. Kentucky vs. Tennessee Injury Report You want more A Sea Of Blue coverage? Then add us to your “Preferred Sources” on Google to get more Kentucky Wildcats news and views.
