item.title: Week 9 Preview: From Wentz We Were
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 13: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a pass in front of Cam Lewis #39 of the Buffalo Bills during the fourth quarter at Highmark Stadium on November 13, 2022 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings return home to U.S. Bank Stadium to face the Buffalo Bills in a rematch of the most memorable regular-season game in years: a thrilling 33-30 overtime road win in 2022. Will the Vikings repeat their magic on Monday Night? Hey, can you believe it’s already November? Time sure does fly, doesn’t it? VIKINGS ON OFFENSE There’s not much more to say that I didn’t cover a few days ago. To be honest, I’m exhausted by it all. Sitting here in Week 9, still sorting this mess out, is really an indictment of Kevin O’Connell and the entire offensive staff. Things need to be fixed, and fast. The Kurt Warner film breakdown video below has been circulating here at the DN and across social media over the past few days. To recap, Kyler Murray has made some nice plays, but he’s missing far too many opportunities. It simply hasn’t been good enough, especially given the weak defenses he’s been facing. Per ESPN’s Bill Barnwell, Murray’s 44.9 QBR through Week 8 ranks just 26th when adjusted for the cupcake units he’s faced. In true Vikings fashion, the schedule was set up beautifully for the offense to find its rhythm before things got tougher, and we flushed the opportunity down the toilet. The last time we faced anything that resembled a “good” defense was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers five weeks ago. As I’m writing this, it’s official: Kevin O’Connell announced that Carson Wentz will start Monday night in place of the injured Murray. Max Brosmer will be the backup. Hmmm. Oh, I’ll just say it: If Wentz plays well, barring an injury or trade, he’ll remain the starter. I believe KOC may have said otherwise, but may I present, as Exhibit 1A, past statements about young quarterbacks and a fella named J.J. McCarthy. Wentz should be an upgrade over his season in the system, given his proven ability to move the ball efficiently. He passed for over 300 yards twice in four starts last year before KOC famously threw him out there against the Chargers in Week 8, while uttering the famous words of Ivan Drago: “If he dies, he dies.” He also, of course, played essentially two games for us this year, going 23-for-39 (59%) for 276 yards (7.08 avg), 3 TDs, and 0 INTs (though a couple of possible ones were dropped). That’s good for a 106.4 QB rating. That’s…okay, but he’ll need to do more if he’s indeed the guy from here on out. Unlike Murray, he does have a proven track record of getting the ball to Justin Jefferson, at least. So that’s something. No doubt Jefferson smiled when he heard the news. Enter the Buffalo Bills, and, will you look at this, another weak defense for us to possibly step on a rake against. Yippee. They rank 23rd in EPA/play, 24th in points allowed (25.9),
item.content:encoded: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 13: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a pass in front of Cam Lewis #39 of the Buffalo Bills during the fourth quarter at Highmark Stadium on November 13, 2022 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings return home to U.S. Bank Stadium to face the Buffalo Bills in a rematch of the most memorable regular-season game in years: a thrilling 33-30 overtime road win in 2022. Will the Vikings repeat their magic on Monday Night? Hey, can you believe it’s already November? Time sure does fly, doesn’t it? VIKINGS ON OFFENSE There’s not much more to say that I didn’t cover a few days ago. To be honest, I’m exhausted by it all. Sitting here in Week 9, still sorting this mess out, is really an indictment of Kevin O’Connell and the entire offensive staff. Things need to be fixed, and fast. The Kurt Warner film breakdown video below has been circulating here at the DN and across social media over the past few days. To recap, Kyler Murray has made some nice plays, but he’s missing far too many opportunities. It simply hasn’t been good enough, especially given the weak defenses he’s been facing. Per ESPN’s Bill Barnwell, Murray’s 44.9 QBR through Week 8 ranks just 26th when adjusted for the cupcake units he’s faced. In true Vikings fashion, the schedule was set up beautifully for the offense to find its rhythm before things got tougher, and we flushed the opportunity down the toilet. The last time we faced anything that resembled a “good” defense was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers five weeks ago. As I’m writing this, it’s official: Kevin O’Connell announced that Carson Wentz will start Monday night in place of the injured Murray. Max Brosmer will be the backup. Hmmm. Oh, I’ll just say it: If Wentz plays well, barring an injury or trade, he’ll remain the starter. I believe KOC may have said otherwise, but may I present, as Exhibit 1A, past statements about young quarterbacks and a fella named J.J. McCarthy. Wentz should be an upgrade over his season in the system, given his proven ability to move the ball efficiently. He passed for over 300 yards twice in four starts last year before KOC famously threw him out there against the Chargers in Week 8, while uttering the famous words of Ivan Drago: “If he dies, he dies.” He also, of course, played essentially two games for us this year, going 23-for-39 (59%) for 276 yards (7.08 avg), 3 TDs, and 0 INTs (though a couple of possible ones were dropped). That’s good for a 106.4 QB rating. That’s…okay, but he’ll need to do more if he’s indeed the guy from here on out. Unlike Murray, he does have a proven track record of getting the ball to Justin Jefferson, at least. So that’s something. No doubt Jefferson smiled when he heard the news. Enter the Buffalo Bills, and, will you look at this, another weak defense for us to possibly step on a rake against. Yippee. They rank 23rd in EPA/play, 24th in points allowed (25.9), 24th in total yards allowed (352.1), and 30th in passing yards allowed (254.7). They’re better against the run (10th), but that may be more about how easily teams have been able to pass against them. Wentz should have opportunities against a porous Bills pass defense, so for goodness’ sake, let’s hope we can finally see some life. The fans need it, and, most of all, an overstressed defense needs it. The pressure to hold teams under 20 to have any shot at winning games, given an offense channeling leather-helmet-era output, has to take its toll. VIKINGS ON DEFENSE Brian Flores and company face what may be their toughest challenge to date in containing Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The Lions are great, but Allen’s mobility and ability to extend plays add an enormous challenge. While he may not be Jahmyr Gibbs, James Cook III is no slouch, averaging 5.1 yards per carry and 101 yards per game. Their receiving corps is solid, if unspectacular. Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, and old Viking nemesis D.J. Moore lead the wideouts, while tight end Dalton Kincaid leads the Bills in receiving yards per game (57.3) and can be a real red-zone menace. But let’s be real: the Bills offense is Josh Allen. For my money, he’s the league’s best quarterback, and he’s playing like it. He’s leading an attack that’s 1st in EPA/play, 2nd in total yards, 2nd in yards per play, 3rd in rushing yards, and 10th in passing yards. They’re also near the top of the league in red zone and 3rd-down percentages, respectively. This is a true strength-vs.-strength battle against the Vikings’ defense. They remain 1st in EPA/play, points per game, success rate allowed, Pass EPA/play, and passing yards allowed. They’re only 2nd in yards allowed per game. What gives, Flores!? Of course, we’ve been vulnerable to the run in a couple of games this year, and the unit’s rankings took a hit after giving up a whopping 230 yards to the Lions last week. We’re now 17th in rushing yards allowed per game and are giving up 4.5 yards per carry. If my concern level for the offense is a 10, I’d put this at a solid 2 right now. They’ll get this straightened out soon enough, but, as noted, this week will bring another challenge. Indeed, you’d think the two priorities for this week would be, first, to keep Cook contained on early downs, which would repeatedly force Allen and the Bills’ offense into the pressure cooker of 3rd-and-long against the blitz and our elite coverage unit. Second, to (as much as possible) keep Allen contained in the pocket in those likely passing situations. If he buys himself time outside the pocket, more often than not you’re toast. Conversely, I’d be shocked if the Bills don’t test our shaky run defense early and often in this one to avoid those very scenarios. In addition, what makes the Bills’ offense so dangerous is their ability to convert 4th-and-short situations with Allen, who, at over 6’ 5” and nearly 240 pounds, is nearly impossible to stuff at the line of scrimmage. This can not only extend drives but also frustrate and demoralize a defense. If we’re to win this one, I can’t see us doing it without creating a turnover or two. The good news is that Allen does suffer from a bit of Stafforditis – i.e., elite QBs who are prone to throwing some head-scratching INTs. Hopefully, the pressure Flores will bring will help. James Cook has also had problems holding onto the ball this year, with four fumbles already, so there’s that, too. PREDICTION Wentz starting gives me a bit more confidence we can pull off the upset, but I can’t, in good conscience, pick the Vikings to win this game until I see something – anything – that resembles consistency from the offense. Scoring 24 points consistently shouldn’t be this difficult with our skill players. Wentz did make the most of the short fields the Packers gave us in Week 1, getting us to 39 points. Sure, there were TD drives of 1 play for 1 yard, 3 plays for 14 yards, and 6 plays for 28 yards. But we also had a 9-play, 83-yard scoring drive! It’s like the ‘98 Vikings and ‘99 Rams rolled into one! Holding Allen and the Bills offense under 20 in this game may require Flores to paint another masterpiece like the Week 17 game against the Lions last year at U.S. Bank Stadium. Can it happen? Absolutely. Will it happen? Ehhh, you can’t count on it. Regardless, it’d be nice not to have to rely on that every week, wouldn’t it? My guess: Wentz injects some much-needed life into the offense, but we come up short. Reverse psychology initiated. Buffalo Bills: 26 Minnesota Vikings: 24

item.title: Anthony Gordon Found Respect At Barcelona, Not Just In England
item.description: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - England Training - Swope Soccer Village, Kansas City, Missouri, U.S. - July 17, 2026 England's Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon during training IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Jay Biggerstaff Anthony Gordon left the Premier League for Barcelona to get ‘respect,’ and he’s got it now . This summer, the 25-year-old English winger arrived from Newcastle United with an initial fee north of €70 million and instantly made an impact. He is already a key part of coach Hansi Flick’s attack alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha. It looks like he finally found the home he needed to really show his talent. Gordon never stopped believing he was meant for the top level, even through the hard times. His boyhood club Everton saw him fight relegation, while a 2021 loan spell took him to Preston North End. He also dealt with scoreless streaks after moving to Newcastle in 2023. But he never lost faith in his own ability to succeed at the highest level. A System That Fits His Style Earlier this season, Gordon spoke about people in England starting to respect ” the quality and IQ that I play with .” His comments were seen as a sign he had not always gotten the recognition he deserved back home. He told ESPN that he did not mean that people were judging him unfairly or that they had a negative view of him. He simply meant they had never seen him in a system that highlights these qualities before. People hadn’t seen him in this kind of system before, which he thinks is helping them appreciate him more. The move to Spain seems to have unlocked a side of his game that the Premier League could not show. Maxime Estève, a defender now at RB Leipzig, told ESPN that Gordon is really good and sharp with a great right foot. Estève said Gordon is great at one-on-ones and wants to beat the right back every time. Was Leaving England Necessary? Was departing the Premier League necessary for him to achieve this? It seems the answer is yes for Gordon. The English game often demands a certain type of physical play that can hide a player’s true brain and skill set. Barcelona offers a different kind of football that lets his IQ shine through on the field. Now a regular starter, he kicked off Tuesday’s UEFA Champions League victory over Aston Villa. Gordon and Barcelona will kick off their LaLiga clash against Atlético Madrid this Sunday at the top of the table. The fans in England might have missed out on seeing his full potential for a few more years. Now they get to watch him thrive on one of the biggest stages in world soccer. The respect he wanted is now being given to him in spades by the Spanish league.

item.title: San Francisco 49ers Announce Christian McCaffrey Decision Before Raiders Game
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up before a game against the Miami Dolphins at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers are 6-1 entering Week 9 of the NFL season as they prepare to take on the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Following Friday’s practice, the team provided several key injury updates and officially ruled out veteran wide receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk, leaving the 49ers offense quite shorthanded. However, they also received positive injury news on star running back Christian McCaffrey, who sustained a mild hamstring injury the last time San Francisco took the field in Week 7. McCaffrey Off Injury Report vs. Raiders In positive news, McCaffrey will be good to go for Sunday’s contest after the 49ers officially removed him from the injury report. He logged back-to-back practices on Thursday and Friday. McCaffrey has played in every game this season and continues to serve as a workhorse in Kyle Shanahan’s high-powered offense. He’ll likely have to shoulder an even greater workload this week with the WR corps so depleted. Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will play Week 9. — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 6, 2026 Earlier this week, McCaffrey revealed that he was caught off guard when he learned the injury was a hamstring issue, but said he “feels great.” “I had no idea [it was a hamstring injury],” McCaffrey said Wednesday. “Sometimes the adrenaline and all these other things can get to you… It wasn’t too bad. Having the bye week was awesome. But now I feel great.” McCaffrey’s 2026 Season With 49ers McCaffrey has appeared in all seven games, recording 84 carries for 389 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. He’s also caught 34 passes for 251 yards. He’s in his 11th NFL season and fifth with the 49ers after San Francisco acquired him from the Carolina Panthers in 2022 in exchange for four draft picks. 49ers Welcoming Back Nick Bosa Another positive sign for the 49ers is that they’ll welcome back star pass rusher Nick Bosa, who has missed several games this season with a calf strain he sustained during practice. Bosa will line up alongside DeForest Buckner, who will make his first start with the 49ers since San Francisco acquired him from the Indianapolis Colts during the bye week. item.content:encoded: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up before a game against the Miami Dolphins at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers are 6-1 entering Week 9 of the NFL season as they prepare to take on the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Following Friday’s practice, the team provided several key injury updates and officially ruled out veteran wide receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk, leaving the 49ers offense quite shorthanded. However, they also received positive injury news on star running back Christian McCaffrey, who sustained a mild hamstring injury the last time San Francisco took the field in Week 7. McCaffrey Off Injury Report vs. Raiders In positive news, McCaffrey will be good to go for Sunday’s contest after the 49ers officially removed him from the injury report. He logged back-to-back practices on Thursday and Friday. McCaffrey has played in every game this season and continues to serve as a workhorse in Kyle Shanahan’s high-powered offense. He’ll likely have to shoulder an even greater workload this week with the WR corps so depleted. Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will play Week 9. — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 6, 2026 Earlier this week, McCaffrey revealed that he was caught off guard when he learned the injury was a hamstring issue, but said he “feels great.” “I had no idea [it was a hamstring injury],” McCaffrey said Wednesday. “Sometimes the adrenaline and all these other things can get to you… It wasn’t too bad. Having the bye week was awesome. But now I feel great.” McCaffrey’s 2026 Season With 49ers McCaffrey has appeared in all seven games, recording 84 carries for 389 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. He’s also caught 34 passes for 251 yards. He’s in his 11th NFL season and fifth with the 49ers after San Francisco acquired him from the Carolina Panthers in 2022 in exchange for four draft picks. 49ers Welcoming Back Nick Bosa Another positive sign for the 49ers is that they’ll welcome back star pass rusher Nick Bosa, who has missed several games this season with a calf strain he sustained during practice. Bosa will line up alongside DeForest Buckner, who will make his first start with the 49ers since San Francisco acquired him from the Indianapolis Colts during the bye week. item.title: NFL Draft big board 2.0: While Jeremiah Smith is No. 1, Arch Manning remains in top 10 trailing Drew Mestemaker

Smith is a gravity-shifter and true math-changer for the offense and for the defense to account for. It’s hard to compare any athlete to Julio Jones, and welp, here we are with Smith. At worst you’re looking at a Josh Gordon-like player. 2. item.dc:creator: Nate Tice
item.content:encoded: Here’s an updated NFL Draft big board as the league approaches its midseason mark and we enter the home stretch of the college football regular season with the playoffs to follow. The conundrum on the timing of this big board is that so many players, especially quarterbacks, could return to school or transfer. This makes me hesitant on how high to put players who could very well be on this board in a year’s time after returning to campus (or transferring to another campus). I’m assuming the players are all declaring for the purposes of this board. With the ever-changing environment of college football and ever-moving targets of player evaluation, we have bob and weave with it. Here’s more than half-a-hundred names now that we’re about halfway home in a wild college football season that has made for a very interesting draft class. 1. Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State A force of nature at receiver, Smith has been a standout player and absurdly productive at every level of his career. He is strong, explosive and has an excellent build that allows him to bounce off tackles and constantly eat up yards after the catch. His power makes him dangerous on inbreakers that allow him to build up speed and get downhill in a hurry, and his speed and burst out of breaks make him dangerous coming out of routes. Smith is a gravity-shifter and true math-changer for the offense and for the defense to account for. It’s hard to compare any athlete to Julio Jones, and welp, here we are with Smith. At worst you’re looking at a Josh Gordon-like player. 2. Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame A long athlete with range and advanced feel for the position, Moore affects a lot of throws with his length, and amplifies it with his body positioning. He has the speed to run with faster wideouts, and the hand-eye coordination and timing to constantly make plays on the football. He showed those skills immediately as a true freshman starter in South Bend. He shines when asked to shadow better WRs and remains an impact player when aligning in the slot. Moore has a chance to be one of the best cornerback prospects I’ve ever studied. 3. Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina A long, lean athlete with agility and Gumby-like bend, Stewart can move around blocks in ways that few can. He still needs refinement with how he uses his hands, but he has a wingspan like a pterodactyl to stave off blockers, and flashes violent stabs and slaps that would unlock a whole new level with more consistency. Stewart’s get-off and twitchiness make him dangerous off the edge or on games as either a penetrator or looper. He’s what teams look for at this position. 4. Jordan Seaton, OT, LSU An easy mover with length and pop with his hands, Seaton can latch on and dominate defenders in the run game. He still has work to do with his hand placement, but Seaton has improved in his polish, eye awareness and overall technique, especially in pass protection. Seaton has the twitch and size to be a valid blindside protector at the next level. 5. Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State Much will be made about Mestemaker’s lack of experience as a starting quarterback at any level (he was a backup in high school and then a walk-on at North Texas). Despite not having the experience or snaps that other typically highly touted quarterbacks have, Mestemaker seems to know how to play the position. He has a good arm that can access all parts of the field and is willing to push the ball from muddy pockets. He can change arm slots and layer the football up and over defenders when needed. Mestemaker is tall and has a long frame that he has started to fill out. He is a solid athlete, albeit not an overwhelming one. But he has a loose arm, is very good at avoiding sacks despite his lack of experience, and can consistently throw on the move, even when working left. Mestemaker is willing to move and work from the pocket and has enough giddyup to work outside of it, too. He has had some inconsistent performances the past few weeks with his decision-making, plays in a very conducive offense that can make his eyes lock in a bit too much (he has yet to take an under-center snap, not a damning thing but worth noting), and hasn’t played the toughest competition so far this season. But Mestemaker has the ability to create throws within and out of structure, and has the size (6-foot-3, 215 pounds) and enough arm to translate to the next level. (Joseph Raines/Yahoo Sports) 6. Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas Simmons is an explosive athlete who is asked to do everything for Texas’ defense. He has shined while pinning his ears back and getting after the passer. He wins with a quick first step and has the ability to run the hoop and turn a corner on offensive tackles. He has been asked to drop into coverage in his college career, and also mirror athletic quarterbacks on passing downs, showing off the front-seven versatility modern defenses love. Simmons’ agility and speed shine in these other areas. 7. Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana An outside receiver with size (6-foot-4, 208 pounds) and long speed, Becker burst onto the scene in a talented wide receiver room and was constantly coming down with big catches in big moments. Becker has strong hands and excellent hand-eye coordination in catching range that allows him to frequently come down with the football. He has long legs, but also shows enough quickness and bend to run a fully developed route tree, which raises his ceiling. 8. Arch Manning, QB, Texas Manning’s 2026 season has been a journey of ups and downs . He still displays the size (6-foot-4, 222 pounds), athleticism, pocket movement and willingness to push the ball that make for an intriguing prospect. That willingness to push the ball, even in too-often mucky pockets, leads to exciting plays but also game-swinging negative ones, too. Manning’s results haven’t always set the world on fire, but he has a style that translates to the next level, namely that aggression and lack of fear throwing into tight windows or tight pockets. When grouped with his speed and arm, he makes for a still-intriguing package at quarterback. More consistent results will help it all feel better. Manning still has to learn to take an easier answer quicker, which to me is to use his legs and rushing ability more often, something he’s tapped back into in recent weeks. His process, while far from perfect, is cleaner when reviewing it on film, especially amid a frustrating Texas offensive ecosystem. 9. Zereoue Williams, OT, Utah Williams is an easy-moving athlete who gets better each week. This former basketball player is an older prospect, but he is still tapping into his potential because of his relative lack of experience at the position and football altogether. He has twitchiness, foot speed and length to develop into a longtime blindside protector. There is also enough strength to be an asset in the run game. 10. Chris Cole, LB, Georgia Cole has sideline-to-sideline range, which isn’t hyperbolic as he actually displays it. He plays with his hair on fire, has the range to cover large swaths of the middle of the field, and shows an ability to come forward in the run game and as a blitzer. Cole’s versatility and four-down ability is what a modern linebacker looks like. 11. Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson Hampton is a big and long corner who can play in zone and impact the game with his size (6-foot-2, 205 pounds) and awareness, but might actually be most unlocked as a player in man coverage situations. He is not overly twitchy, yet he’s a smooth athlete who can fluidly get in and out of his turns. His size, foot speed and ball skills give him a chance at being a lockdown player on the outside at the next level. He reminds me a bit of James Bradberry. 12. Austin Simmons, QB, Missouri Note: Simmons has reportedly “re-signed” with Missouri for the 2027 season on Friday, but with a caveat that he can still explore the draft after the season. I have kept his ranking and report as is. Si

item.title: Former Dodgers Hitting Coach Aaron Bates Explains Why He Left
item.description: Former Los Angeles Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates opened up about the behind-the-scenes details of his departure. After 12 years with the Dodgers, Bates is moving on after contract negotiations stalled. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) How Aaron Bates and the Dodgers parted ways According to Bates, he received a multi-year offer, which he told Maddie Lee of the LA Times was “not a competitive offer.” He rejected the offer and expected talks to continue, but no other follow-up offer came. “Basically, they said, ‘I think we should go our separate ways,” Bates told The LA Times. “I was just very taken aback, in a sense, by that.” Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes did not comment on the talks, but told The Times that he wished “nothing but the best for Bates and his family.” Sep 1, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes during the game against the St. Louis Cardinals at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Reflecting on how things played out, Bates didn’t seem to hold any bitter feelings about how it worked out. “Processing it, I think that there’s always a time and a place, and I think that things run their course,” Bates said to Lee. “But I have nothing but amazing things to say about the Dodgers organization and people. “My kids grew up Dodgers, and I grew up a Dodger, as a coach. It’s just unfortunate the way it’s worked out towards these last few days.” Feb 20, 2019; Glendale, AZ, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers assistant hitting coach Aaron Bates poses for a portrait during media day at Camelback Ranch. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters) What is next for Aaron Bates and the Dodgers? With experience in a highly esteemed organization like the Dodgers and as a three-time champion, Bates should land on his feet easily. In fact, he told the Times that he is already speaking with other teams. “I’m talking to many different teams, and we’re kind of working through some things, and I’ll leave it at that for now,” he said. “But it’s exciting times in that sense.” Regarding the Dodgers, they will likely now either promote internally or bring in someone from another organization, but either way, there will be a fresh voice on the coaching staff. Changes on successful teams can be tough, but after a disappointing NLCS exit in which the offense went cold, shaking things up could help.

item.title: Insider Delivers Harsh Reality on Jaguars Trade Deadline Plans
item.description: Jacksonville Jaguars general manager James Gladstone speaks to the media during the NFL Scouting Combine. Getty CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Derrick Brown #95 of the Carolina Panthers warms up prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty The Jacksonville Jaguars are reportedly interested in adding a defensive tackle at the trade deadline. They are looking for a big-name addition that could move the needle, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. However, the market appears to be drying up in front of them, according to Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated. Breer notes that the Jaguars were interested in Jeffery Simmons and DeForest Buckner, but being in the same division as both hurt their odds of making a move. He goes on to mention that the other options around the league that are big names are not as likely to be moved. “Washington’s Daron Payne was drawing interest before he got hurt,” noted Breer. “To this point, the Eagles have said no to teams on Moro Ojomo (more on him in a bit), and the Dolphins have done the same with Zach Sieler. The pie-in-the-sky swing for someone to take, in the Simmons aftermath, might be for Panthers star Derrick Brown. That would be very expensive, though, with Carolina not actively looking to move him.” So, the next four names that are worth targeting for the Jaguars appear to either be off the table or at a price range that is hard to reach. Jacksonville Jaguars Remain in Pursuit of Defensive Lineman at Trade Deadline Getty Derrick Brown #95 of the Carolina Panthers Breer added that there are a few lower-end names that are coming up as options for the Jaguars. “Grover Stewart’s an option, with the Saints’ Davon Godchaux and Nathan Shepherd, Patriots’ Christian Barmore and Panthers’ Bobby Brown III others who’ve come up in trade talks,” added Breer. However, those names do not move the needle in the way that Ojomo, Brown or Sieler would. It is worth noting that John Shipley of Jaguars OnSI thinks that their most recent win is going to cause the team to meet the Panthers’ demands and pay up for a big name. “I think the Jaguars will add two defenders by the end of the deadline,” wrote Shipley after the Jags’ Week 9 win. “My best guess is that it comes at the defensive tackle and safety positions, though edge is always a spot to watch due to the depth of pass-rushers who could be had. My ultimate guess is they add Derrick Brown.” While safety is also an option, all of the smoke continues to build at nose tackle. Jaguars Need Defensive Line Help The Jaguars’ defensive line was always a problem, and the team was looking for help before Week 8. However, in Week 8, they lost their best run defender and top nose tackle, DaVon Hamilton. With Hamilton out, the Jags went from exploring options to being all-in on adding a big name. The team does not play another game before the trade deadl

item.title: Broncos Roster Move Spells Excellent Sign for Talanoa Hufanga
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Talanoa Hufanga #9 of the Denver Broncos during warm up before the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Getty The Denver Broncos made what some consider to be a surprise move when they released safety Taylor Rapp on Friday. Despite starting the season on the practice squad, Rapp played a starting role on defense over the past three weeks, and prior to his third start in Week 8, was elevated to the active roster. Now no longer having need of the 28-year old’s services implies that safety Talanoa Hufanga; who did not practice on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday; is good to go for Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Mild surprise! A good sign that Hufanga is good to go for Sunday tho. https://t.co/l8De2L6wIJ — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 6, 2026 Taylor Rapp Cut; Suggests Talanoa Hufanga Will Play Week 9 The former Buffalo Bill had been covering Hufanga’s duties whilst the two-time All-Pro safety dealt with an ankle injury over the past few weeks, alongside fellow starter Brandon Jones . Officially, Hufanga is “questionable”, but the timing of the announcement feels inescapable; the Broncos surely would not release their interim starter for the past three weeks without a high degree of confidence that their top guy was ready to go. Especially given the two next men up, Devon Key and Tycen Anderson , have four combined NFL starts between them. Even then, two of Key’s starts were in Week 6 and Week 7, during which he played less than 40% of snaps on defense, with Rapp and Jones seeing the majority of the action. Anderson himself is mostly a special teams contributor, so if Hufanga is not ready, then the Broncos will have no full-time safety option behind Jones and Key. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Broncos Roster Move Spells Excellent Sign for Talanoa Hufanga appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: 'Two-headed monster' on point for Hope College women's basketball this season
item.description: HOLLAND - The Hope College women's basketball team has been a national powerhouse for decades. Designed to win with defense, this year's version of the Flying Dutch has two experienced point guards leading the way on both sides of the ball. Starting point guard Terin Maynard pushes the pace, drives to the basket and anchors the perimeter defense. While most teams lose quite a bit when a backup point guard goes in. For Hope, there is hardly a noticeable difference when Josie DeSmit checks in. The duo led Hope to a 72-65 win over Wisconsin-Platteville on Friday, Nov. 6, at DeVos Fieldhouse to open the season - both scoring career highs in the process. More: Hope College women's basketball reloads 2026-27 roster after run to Sweet 16 Maynard scored a career-high 20 points to go along with six assists, while DeSmit had a career-high 15 points with three steals. Leah Richards had 15 points and eight rebounds. "They were really good today," Hope coach Brian Morehouse said. "Josie is good enough to start and played her role very well. It gives us a two-headed monster and that is really hard on other teams." The game was close in the fourth quarter and Morehouse chose to play both point guards together. DeSmit nailed a 3-pointer, then scored another basket to make it 64-54 with 4:50 to go. "We showed our resilience and found a way to stick together and do the dirty work," Maynard said. The Pioneers closed the gap again and Maynard took over with three-point play and a basket in the paint to make it 71-63 with 2:26 to go. "We withstood 11 from 3 and gutted it out. We switched our defenses up and our defense was really good, but they had a lot of good shots in the last seconds of the shot clock. We played both of them together and if they can rebound a little more we will see that some more." It was a fun change. "We push each other every day in practice. I get to go up against the best defender in the MIAA. We feed off each other well and have some good chemistry," DeSmit said. "We both have our own strengths. Those differences help a ton on the court." This is the second year they have been the top two point guards on the roster. "It has been awesome to have her. When we do both go out there, we have the confidence in each other and can read each other," Maynard said. "We found a way to do that well." It could key another strong season for the Flying Dutch. "We have a lot of potential this year," Maynard said. "We have great new freshman who have grown our circle and we are starting better than we finished last year. We can only go up." Contact sports editor Dan D’Addona at Dan.D’Addona@hollandsentinel.com. Follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter @DanDAddona or Facebook @HollandSentinelSport s. This article originally appeared on The Holland Sentinel: 'Two-headed monster' on point for Hope College women's basketball this season

It gives us a two-headed monster and that is really hard on other teams." The game was close in the fourth quarter and Morehouse chose to play both point guards together. DeSmit nailed a 3-pointer, then scored another basket to make it 64-54 with 4:50 to go. "We showed our resilience and found a way to stick together and do the dirty work," Maynard said. The Pioneers closed the gap again and Maynard took over with three-point play and a basket in the paint to make it 71-63 with 2:26 to go. "We withstood 11 from 3 and gutted it out. We switched our defenses up and our defense was really good, but they had a lot of good shots in the last seconds of the shot clock. We played both of them together and if they can rebound a little more we will see that some more." It was a fun change. "We push each other every day in practice. I get to go up against the best defender in the MIAA. We feed off each other well and have some good chemistry," DeSmit said. "We both have our own strengths. Those differences help a ton on the court." This is the second year they have been the top two point guards on the roster. "It has been awesome to have her. When we do both go out there, we have the confidence in each other and can read each other," Maynard said. "We found a way to do that well." It could key another strong season for the Flying Dutch. "We have a lot of potential this year," Maynard said. "We have great new freshman who have grown our circle and we are starting better than we finished last year. We can only go up." item.title: Claudio Castagnoli Calls League of Legends ‘the Best Sport to Watch’
item.description: Pro Wrestler for AEW Claudio Castagnoli makes an announcement at League of Legends Worlds 2026 QuarterFinals Day 4 on Friday, November 06, 2026 in Allen, Texas. ALLEN, Texas — Finding new hobbies can be difficult, especially when you’re on the road for 300-plus days a year. Pro wrestler Claudio Castagnoli has always liked gaming. Still, he didn’t start playing League of Legends until a showmatch crossover between his former company (WWE) and Riot Games introduced him to it. It’s been eight years since that showmatch, and a lot has changed. He works for a new company (All Elite Wrestling) and doesn’t have enough time to play as many games as he’d like. But he still finds time to watch League of Legends, including stopping by the World Championship quarterfinal match between Korea’s T1 and France’s Karmine Corp. “League of Legends is the best sport to watch,” he said. “It’s so exciting.” Castagnoli appeared on the live broadcast, where he announced the teams as they entered the arena and was also interviewed. For him, the chance to see the League of Legends World Championships is too good to pass up. Despite his world travels this year, including Mexico, the United Kingdom, and Japan, he hasn’t been to Korea to soak up the heart of esports. “I’m sure [League of Legends is] kind of popular over there,” Castagnoli said with a smirk. He compared the League of Legends crowd at the event to the rabid fans who attend AEW shows. He’s been to a League of Legends event in China and said the experience is similar to the events he works. “It’s the passion of the fans for the team, for the game, and how they show it,” Castagnoli said. “They have signs. They come early. They dress up. They wear jerseys. They show their passion and pride.” More importantly, he compared the title and pro wrestling as two industries that have immense lore and histories that fans can track for years. Take weekly AEW television and the stories that advance week to week, and compare it to traditional media such as Arcane . Both build character lore and offer ways to attract fans while providing more content. The thing, however, he said that was also similar was the idea that all it takes is exposure to the game and environment to get people hooked. “There are a lot of people that are like, ‘I’m not really into it,’” Castagnoli said. “I’m like, ‘Well, if you come to a live show, you’ll be a fan just because you see it.’ Once you play, and I feel like, especially once you play with your friends, it just becomes so much more fun because we can all watch Worlds at the highest level.” He also offered advice to new League of Legends fans. “Don’t try to imitate because it’s quite frustrating,” Castagnoli said. While Castagnoli can make physical feats seem effortless, such as his trademark giant swing, micro movements with a mouse and maneuvering around the Rift (the name of League of Legends’ map) offer a different challenge. “I’m the worst. I misclick and click the wrong buttons,” he said.

item.title: Mutfwang: Educated Nigerians masterminding corruption, institutional decay
item.description: …says professionals behind major governance failures …challenges graduates to choose integrity over wealth By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has accused educated Nigerians of masterminding some of the country’s most damaging corruption scandals, financial fraud and institutional abuses, saying the nation’s governance crisis is not a result of a shortage of intellectual capacity but a failure of conscience. Mutfwang said some of the most sophisticated acts of financial fraud, contract manipulation, money laundering and subversion of public institutions were perpetrated by people whose academic qualifications and professional expertise should ordinarily be deployed for national development. The governor spoke on Friday in Abuja while delivering the convocation lecture at the 15th Convocation Ceremony of Veritas University. In his lecture titled, “Building the Nigeria We Want: The Role of the Educated Mind,” he warned that education without moral discipline had become a dangerous instrument against the country’s progress. He challenged the graduating students to rethink the purpose of university education, insisting that academic certificates and intellectual brilliance would amount to little if deployed for selfish interests at the expense of society. According to him, Nigeria’s development challenges cannot be blamed entirely on inadequate manpower or lack of expertise, as many individuals responsible for undermining public institutions are highly educated and professionally trained. Describing the situation as an uncomfortable reality the country must confront, Mutfwang said some of Nigeria’s most entrenched governance failures were products of educated minds. He said: “Indeed, I make an uncomfortable observation: the afflictions I diagnosed earlier, prebendalism, the privatisation of public office, grand corruption, the capture of institutions, are almost never the work of illiterate minds. They are overwhelmingly executed by educated minds. “The contract, the doctored account, the laundered fund, the ingenious evasion of law. All these are the signatures of trained minds. This is the paradox we must confront. The educated mind is at once our greatest hope, and when corrupted, it becomes our most sophisticated danger.” The governor also cited internet fraudsters, popularly known as Yahoo boys, as an example of intelligence deployed in the wrong direction, arguing that criminal ingenuity reflected a lack of moral restraint rather than an absence of intelligence. “The Yahoo boy is certainly not a derelict. He is a work of intelligence, but intelligence wrongly applied,” he said. item.content:encoded: …says professionals behind major governance failures …challenges graduates to choose integrity over wealth By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has accused educated Nigerians of masterminding some of the country’s most damaging corruption scandals, financial fraud and institutional abuses, saying the nation’s governance crisis is not a result of a shortage of intellectual capacity but a failure of conscience. Mutfwang said some of the most sophisticated acts of financial fraud, contract manipulation, money laundering and subversion of public institutions were perpetrated by people whose academic qualifications and professional expertise should ordinarily be deployed for national development. The governor spoke on Friday in Abuja while delivering the convocation lecture at the 15th Convocation Ceremony of Veritas University. In his lecture titled, “Building the Nigeria We Want: The Role of the Educated Mind,” he warned that education without moral discipline had become a dangerous instrument against the country’s progress. He challenged the graduating students to rethink the purpose of university education, insisting that academic certificates and intellectual brilliance would amount to little if deployed for selfish interests at the expense of society. According to him, Nigeria’s development challenges cannot be blamed entirely on inadequate manpower or lack of expertise, as many individuals responsible for undermining public institutions are highly educated and professionally trained. Describing the situation as an uncomfortable reality the country must confront, Mutfwang said some of Nigeria’s most entrenched governance failures were products of educated minds. He said: “Indeed, I make an uncomfortable observation: the afflictions I diagnosed earlier, prebendalism, the privatisation of public office, grand corruption, the capture of institutions, are almost never the work of illiterate minds. They are overwhelmingly executed by educated minds. “The contract, the doctored account, the laundered fund, the ingenious evasion of law. All these are the signatures of trained minds. This is the paradox we must confront. The educated mind is at once our greatest hope, and when corrupted, it becomes our most sophisticated danger.” The governor also cited internet fraudsters, popularly known as Yahoo boys, as an example of intelligence deployed in the wrong direction, arguing that criminal ingenuity reflected a lack of moral restraint rather than an absence of intelligence. “The Yahoo boy is certainly not a derelict. He is a work of intelligence, but intelligence wrongly applied,” he said. Mutfwang maintained that Nigeria had no shortage of brilliant citizens, noting the achievements of Nigerians across different professions and on international platforms. However, he lamented that the country had failed to translate its abundant intellectual resources into responsible leadership, accountable governance and sustainable development. He urged the graduating students not to measure success solely by their earning capacity, professional positions or social standing, but by the extent to which their knowledge improved the lives of others. According to him, intellectual capacity must be matched with conscience, warning that an educated person without moral discipline could inflict greater damage on society than someone without formal education. “Knowledge tells you what you can do, but conscience tells you what you should do. An educated mind without a formed conscience is not an asset to any nation. It is a very efficient danger,” he declared. The governor identified integrity, responsibility and competence as three critical attributes Nigeria needed from its educated population to overcome its development challenges. He explained that responsibility required citizens to accept the consequences of their decisions rather than hide behind claims of good intentions. Citing the principles in The Ethics of Responsibility, Mutfwang said national development required individuals willing to take ownership of the outcomes of their actions. He described the Nigeria of his aspiration as a country where hospitals delivered quality healthcare, courts dispensed justice, schools provided meaningful education and public office holders regarded their positions as opportunities to serve rather than avenues for personal enrichment. “The Nigeria we want is a nation of institutions that work, where the hospital heals, where the courts deliver justice, where the schools teach, and public office serves truly the public. “It is a nation where merit is rewarded and mediocrity is not enthroned, where security is felt in the farm, in the market, at home, where prosperity is shared rather than captured, and where leaders understand office as stewardship and not as a spoil,” he said. Mutfwang, who reaffirmed his belief in Nigeria’s unity, said the country’s ethnic, linguistic and cultural diversity should be regarded as an opportunity to build a stronger nation rather than an excuse for division. He also disagreed with the notion that the 1914 amalgamation was necessarily a mistake, arguing that Nigeria’s diverse peoples had a common responsibility to determine the country’s future. “I do not share the view that the amalgamation of 1914 was necessarily a mistake. I acknowledge our extraordinary diversity and the fact that our peoples have distinct histories, distinct languages and distinct identities. Yet I believe God has a purpose for bringing us together. Our responsibility is to decide what we will make of this country,” he said. The governor further expressed concern over the withdrawal of credible and competent Nigerians from politics and public service, warning that their absence was worsening the country’s governance challenges. He urged educated Nigerians to stop abandoning the public space to individuals who might not possess the integrity and commitment required to serve the country. “One reason our public square so often disappoints is that too many good people have vacated it, abandoning it to those least fit to occupy it. “Government and public service are not dirty words. They are the arenas in which the future of a nation is decided. If the best remain outside, the worst will not,” he warned. Mutfwang stressed that nation-building was not the exclusive responsibility of elected officials or political appointees, but required the everyday commitment and responsible decisions of citizens across different professions. item.title: 2027: APGA adopts Tinubu, flags off nationwide campaign
item.description: …Soludo cites South-East projects, urges strategic voting By Steve Oko The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) has adopted President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, with Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, saying the decision was informed by the need for progressive forces to work together. Soludo made the declaration on Friday while flagging off APGA’s nationwide election campaign at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, Anambra State, where the party unveiled more than 253 candidates contesting various elective positions across the country. The governor, who is APGA’s National Leader, said the decision to support Tinubu was consistent with the party’s political tradition, recalling that APGA had similarly adopted former President Goodluck Jonathan in the 2011 and 2015 presidential elections. He said the party’s support for Tinubu was also informed by what he described as the Federal Government’s commitment to the South-East, particularly in infrastructure development. “Today, as we unveil our campaign as the foremost progressive party in Nigeria, we are also officially adopting President Bola Tinubu as the presidential candidate of APGA. “We did it in 2011 and 2015 for President Jonathan. We are repeating it in 2027 because progressives are working together to support a President who loves Ndi Igbo and Ndi Anambra,” Soludo declared. Citing the dualisation and rehabilitation of the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway and other federal projects in the region, the governor urged voters to approach the 2027 elections with political pragmatism rather than sentiment. He said voting decisions should be guided by tangible benefits, enlightened self-interest and strategic political considerations capable of advancing the interests of the South-East. Soludo also charged APGA candidates and members to intensify grassroots mobilisation through door-to-door campaigns, assuring them that he would personally join the candidates in soliciting votes. He expressed confidence in the party’s electoral prospects, urging voters to distinguish between reason and emotion ahead of the January 16 and February 6, 2027 elections. At the event, Soludo presented party flags to 44 APGA candidates contesting legislative seats in Anambra State. The candidates comprised three senatorial candidates, 11 House of Representatives candidates and 30 State House of Assembly candidates. Earlier, APGA National Chairman, Barrister Sly Ezeokenwa, commended Soludo for what he described as transparent and competitive party primaries conducted in compliance with electoral laws. Ezeokenwa attributed the influx of new members into the party to Soludo’s people-oriented policies, describing Anambra as APGA’s political stronghold. He expressed confidence that the party would record a decisive victory in the forthcoming elections. The post 2027: APGA adopts Tinubu, flags off nationwide campaign appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Ebonyi youths march against political violence, intimidation
item.description: …demand peaceful campaigns, protection of opposition parties By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki A group under the aegis of Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy has staged a peaceful road march in Ebonyi State to protest alleged political violence, harassment and intimidation of opposition political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group condemned reported attacks and killings of opposition party members in parts of the state, insisting that all political parties must be allowed to campaign and exercise their democratic rights without fear. Addressing participants during the march, Nollywood actor, Steve Rostick Eze, said the demonstration was aimed at promoting peaceful campaigns and elections while condemning attacks on opposition parties. He urged youths to shun violence and mobilise voters to support candidates of their choice without fear, favour or intimidation. Eze also called on security agencies to provide adequate protection for all political parties and ensure compliance with electoral rules and the rule of law. “We have gathered today to march for peace, march for freedom, march for democracy. It is time that we say no to violence. It is time that we say no to oppression. It is time for us to take back peace, freedom in our state, Ebonyi State,” he said. The National President of Anyigaemeya Youth Assembly, Mr. Nnanna Nwangene, also condemned political intimidation and thuggery, declaring his support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid and the governorship ambition of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Dr. Ifeanyichukwu Odii, in 2027. Nwangene said the march was to demonstrate that Ebonyi belonged to all political parties and that citizens had the constitutional right to freely express their political preferences. He said: “We have gathered to tell the whole world and the Ebonyians that Ebonyi belongs to all of us. Ebonyi is not a one-party state. Ebonyi belongs to all political parties. “We want a freedom where all political parties will be allowed to participate in a peaceful campaign without being attacked. We want every Ebonyian to understand that we are marching for peace.” He called on opposition parties to be allowed to exercise their political rights without harassment, adding that political differences should not lead to violence. item.content:encoded: …demand peaceful campaigns, protection of opposition parties By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki A group under the aegis of Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy has staged a peaceful road march in Ebonyi State to protest alleged political violence, harassment and intimidation of opposition political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group condemned reported attacks and killings of opposition party members in parts of the state, insisting that all political parties must be allowed to campaign and exercise their democratic rights without fear. Addressing participants during the march, Nollywood actor, Steve Rostick Eze, said the demonstration was aimed at promoting peaceful campaigns and elections while condemning attacks on opposition parties. He urged youths to shun violence and mobilise voters to support candidates of their choice without fear, favour or intimidation. Eze also called on security agencies to provide adequate protection for all political parties and ensure compliance with electoral rules and the rule of law. “We have gathered today to march for peace, march for freedom, march for democracy. It is time that we say no to violence. It is time that we say no to oppression. It is time for us to take back peace, freedom in our state, Ebonyi State,” he said. The National President of Anyigaemeya Youth Assembly, Mr. Nnanna Nwangene, also condemned political intimidation and thuggery, declaring his support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid and the governorship ambition of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Dr. Ifeanyichukwu Odii, in 2027. Nwangene said the march was to demonstrate that Ebonyi belonged to all political parties and that citizens had the constitutional right to freely express their political preferences. He said: “We have gathered to tell the whole world and the Ebonyians that Ebonyi belongs to all of us. Ebonyi is not a one-party state. Ebonyi belongs to all political parties. “We want a freedom where all political parties will be allowed to participate in a peaceful campaign without being attacked. We want every Ebonyian to understand that we are marching for peace.” He called on opposition parties to be allowed to exercise their political rights without harassment, adding that political differences should not lead to violence. Another youth leader, Prince Igwe Udemanta, warned against a recurrence of election-related violence in the state, recalling the loss of lives during previous election cycles, particularly in 2003 and 2007. He said Ebonyi should not become a state associated with bloodshed, stressing that political disagreements must not degenerate into violence. Udemanta urged supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), APGA and other political parties to conduct their activities peacefully. He said the people should be allowed to decide who governs them through the ballot rather than intimidation or violence. He added that political violence could affect anyone, warning that no individual or political group had a monopoly of it. Also speaking, a media aide to the PDP governorship candidate, Dr. Jerry Uhuo, said the march was intended to remind political actors of the need to preserve the peace and development for which Ebonyi State was created. Uhuo recalled that the state’s creation followed years of agitation and sacrifices, arguing that the gains should not be undermined by election-related violence. He said every citizen had the right to determine who became governor, senator or occupied other elective positions, insisting that no individual should be prevented from exercising that right through intimidation. Referring to previous election-related killings, he questioned the justification for shedding blood in the pursuit of political power. “Do you seek for power with people’s blood? No! If you kill the people you want to govern, who are you going to govern?” he asked. Uhuo further alleged that political interests and influential stakeholders had constrained the administration of Governor Francis Nwifuru, a claim he made while calling for a change in the state’s political leadership. He said the 2027 elections should be peaceful and urged voters to prioritise competence and capacity when choosing their leaders. “Election is not war. People should remember that there is life after politics,” he said. Other speakers, including Mark Onuh, also condemned alleged attacks on opposition political parties and called for an atmosphere that would allow all political actors to campaign freely. The participants urged security agencies and relevant authorities to protect citizens and ensure that the 2027 electoral process was peaceful and inclusive. item.title: CAFA urges unified policies to grow Africa’s fashion economy to $500bn
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku The Confederation of African Fashion,CAFA, has called on African countries to harmonise their fashion policies, strengthen intellectual property protection and invest in local manufacturing as part of efforts to grow the continent’s fashion economy to $500 billion. The President of CAFA, Professor Lai Labode, made the call during the unveiling of the joint stand of the organisation and the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy at the ongoing CANEX WKND 2026. Labode said Africa had no shortage of creative talent but lacked the structures and policies needed to translate its creative potential into economic value. “In Africa, we don’t have a shortage of talent. What Africa needs is structure. Money always follows structure,” he said. He said the African Fashion Industry Growth Charter, developed by CAFA, was built around 10 pillars designed to address challenges across the fashion value chain, including policy harmonisation, raw material cultivation and processing, intellectual property protection, counterfeiting, logistics and market access. Labode stressed the need for African countries to process their raw materials locally instead of exporting them in largely unprocessed forms, arguing that local value addition would create jobs and retain more wealth within the continent. Using cotton production as an example, he compared Brazil’s reported $5.3 billion cotton exports with China’s earnings from cotton production and processing, saying Africa needed to build its own processing capacity to compete more effectively. He also identified intellectual property protection as a major priority, noting that African designers and creative businesses needed stronger systems to protect their original works from counterfeiting and unauthorised use. On market access, Labode disclosed plans to establish about 10 African fashion houses across the continent, alongside outlets in New York, Paris, Milan and London, to promote African designers and connect them with international markets. He called for common intellectual property rules and standards across African countries, warning that fragmented systems could weaken the continent’s competitiveness. The CAFA president also urged member states to support the intellectual property framework under the African Continental Free Trade Area, saying the relevant protocol annexes had been passed in February 2026 but required wider participation by African countries. Speaking in the same vein, the Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, identified private-sector partnerships, policy development and infrastructure as essential to strengthening Nigeria’s fashion industry. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Benjamin Njoku The Confederation of African Fashion,CAFA, has called on African countries to harmonise their fashion policies, strengthen intellectual property protection and invest in local manufacturing as part of efforts to grow the continent’s fashion economy to $500 billion. The President of CAFA, Professor Lai Labode, made the call during the unveiling of the joint stand of the organisation and the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy at the ongoing CANEX WKND 2026. Labode said Africa had no shortage of creative talent but lacked the structures and policies needed to translate its creative potential into economic value. “In Africa, we don’t have a shortage of talent. What Africa needs is structure. Money always follows structure,” he said. He said the African Fashion Industry Growth Charter, developed by CAFA, was built around 10 pillars designed to address challenges across the fashion value chain, including policy harmonisation, raw material cultivation and processing, intellectual property protection, counterfeiting, logistics and market access. Labode stressed the need for African countries to process their raw materials locally instead of exporting them in largely unprocessed forms, arguing that local value addition would create jobs and retain more wealth within the continent. Using cotton production as an example, he compared Brazil’s reported $5.3 billion cotton exports with China’s earnings from cotton production and processing, saying Africa needed to build its own processing capacity to compete more effectively. He also identified intellectual property protection as a major priority, noting that African designers and creative businesses needed stronger systems to protect their original works from counterfeiting and unauthorised use. On market access, Labode disclosed plans to establish about 10 African fashion houses across the continent, alongside outlets in New York, Paris, Milan and London, to promote African designers and connect them with international markets. He called for common intellectual property rules and standards across African countries, warning that fragmented systems could weaken the continent’s competitiveness. The CAFA president also urged member states to support the intellectual property framework under the African Continental Free Trade Area, saying the relevant protocol annexes had been passed in February 2026 but required wider participation by African countries. Speaking in the same vein, the Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, identified private-sector partnerships, policy development and infrastructure as essential to strengthening Nigeria’s fashion industry. Musawa said the collaboration with CAFA should translate into tangible economic benefits, particularly job creation, while promoting African unity, cultural pride and soft power. She disclosed that the ministry was working towards establishing an intellectual property policy to protect fashion designers across Nigeria, irrespective of their backgrounds. “Partnerships, the policies, and hubs, it is very important to put us to capacity-building, and that can only happen through infrastructure,” she said. The minister added that the ministry was working to establish creative hubs across the country to support capacity building, stimulate economic growth and create employment opportunities. Beyond government policies and investment, discussions at the CAFA stand highlighted the need to build sustainable fashion businesses through financial literacy, proper business structures and production-cost management. Series of discussions at the event also highlighted the importance of preserving African textile heritage while adapting traditional designs to contemporary markets. Participants identified technology as an important tool for improving garment sizing, production consistency and quality standards, particularly as African designers seek to serve international markets. They also emphasised the need to document traditional textile knowledge and protect the cultural meanings associated with indigenous patterns and designs. Speaking on local patronage, Labode said Nigerians were increasingly embracing traditional fabrics such as adire and aso-oke rather than relying exclusively on Western-style clothing. He said Africa was already exporting about $15 billion worth of apparel and related products but could achieve greater economic returns by strengthening local production and consumption. He encouraged Africans to incorporate locally made clothing into their everyday dressing, saying the continent needed to place greater value on its own fashion and textile products. The four-day gathering which gathers creatives, entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers and industry stakeholders from Africa and the diaspora to explore opportunities across the creative and cultural industries will round off tomorrow, with cultural activities and a Legends football. item.title: OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO
item.description: OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion in a new round of funding that has raised another $11 billion, according to Bloomberg . item.title: CANEX WKND 2026 lights up Lagos as Davido, Fally Ipupa, Flavour headline star-studded concert tonight
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku & Tony-Okafor Favour The 2026 edition of Creative Africa Nexus Weekend, CANEX WKND, which opened at the Professor Wole Soyinka Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos on Thursday, continues this evening with a blockbuster concert. Headlining the night are some of Africa’s biggest music stars, including Nigeria’s Davido, Congolese sensation Fally Ipupa, Flavour, Cali-Ber Tha Grime, Sabrina Francis and Nigerian DJ duo Wanni X Handi. The concert will bring together performers from Africa and the Caribbean for an evening of live music, rhythm and cultural celebration. The four-day gathering, themed “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World”, has brought the once moribund Arts Theatre back to life. It convened leading voices from film, music, fashion, sport, publishing, gastronomy and business to advance trade, investment and commercial opportunities across Africa’s creative economy. The opening day featured a series of masterclasses and sessions, including Building Your Brand as an Independent Artist, Podcasting for Success, Fashion Masterclass: Building Profitable Fashion Brands, and Building Sustainable Business Models in the Performing Arts. In attendance were Vice-President Kassim Shettima, Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Afreximbank President and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Dr George Elombi; Nigeria’s Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole; and African Continental Free Trade Area Secretary-General, Wamkele Mene. Other dignitaries included the Minister of Arts, Culture, Tourism, and the Creative Economy for Nigeria, Hon Hannatu Musa Musawa; Mrs Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President of Intra-African Trade and Export Development at Afreximbank; Hon Ginger Moxey, Minister for Grand Bahama; Emmy Award-winning actor Uzo Aduba; filmmaker Funke Akindele; and actors Richard Mofe-Damijo and Thuso Mbedu among other dignitaries. Speaking while declaring the programme open, Shettima said the world will eventually hear about the can-do spirit of African women. He commended Afreximbank for committing $2 billion to Africa’s creative industries by 2027, noting that the industry is not just about entertainment, but also serious economic infrastructure. Shettima took the audience down memory lane, recalling almost 50 years ago when the same Arts Theatre hosted the second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture, FESTAC ’77, where the Black World declared through music, dance, literature and art that “our culture was not just a footnote to history, but the very core within it. “In 1977, we came to celebrate our culture. In 2024, we are here to capitalize it,” he said. He urged Africans to be proud of who they are without asking for anything in return. The post CANEX WKND 2026 lights up Lagos as Davido, Fally Ipupa, Flavour headline star-studded concert tonight appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Bimbo Ademoye shines in dual roles
item.description: By Ammah Sarah Bimbo Ademoye is stepping into one of the biggest moments of her career as she takes on a dual role in the highly anticipated film,”The Secret Lives of Baba Segi’s Wives.” The actress is not only starring in the film, she is also serving as an Executive Producer, a move that shows her growth from screen star to power player behind the scenes. In the film, Ademoye plays the character Iya Femi, a role fans are already excited to see her bring to life. Sharing the news with her followers, Ademoye expressed her excitement about being part of the production, describing it as a special experience from start to finish. The film has already started making waves internationally. From Toronto to London, it has enjoyed screenings at two prestigious Oscar-qualifying film festivals, earning attention from global audiences and critics. Now, the excitement is moving to Africa. The film is set to celebrate its premiere in Africa November 29, an event fans across the continent have been waiting for. After the premiere, it will be released in Nigeria and other West African countries on December 4, and in the UK, USA, and Canada on December 11. The post Bimbo Ademoye shines in dual roles appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Toke Makinwa takes fans down memory lane with live podcast
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku Still basking in the glow of her surprise 32nd birthday party, Toke Makinwa is taking her fans on a nostalgic trip back to where it all began. The Nigerian media personality and actress has announced plans to stage a live podcast of the first episode of her live show on November 21 in Lagos. Taking to Instagram to share the news, the former OAP wrote: “A little nostalgic trip down memory lane… We have come so far. I remember my very first episode. Let’s meet, let’s connect, November 21, in Lagos.” Her birthday on November 3 was anything but quiet. Friends and well-wishers pulled off a surprise party for the queen, and videos from the celebration showed her enjoying every moment with her circle. Though she admitted she wasn’t easily surprised, this time she dofed her cap for her friends. “I had the longest birthday blues, did not want to do anything on my birthday which is not like me and I am so thankful my circle did not listen,” she wrote. “She had two outfits and when everyone kept cancelling from coming to my house, I agreed to go to dinner at @maisonprivelagos. “I walked in totally surprised. I had the best dinner.” The post Toke Makinwa takes fans down memory lane with live podcast appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Man unexpectedly recovers from a knife wound through his eye and brain
item.description: A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull. Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5) , indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5). In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. So, they swiftly sedated and intubated him. They put him on prophylactic treatments for bacterial infections, including tetanus. Then they used images to see what was going on in his head. Read full article Comments

item.title: Starlink Mobile: All the news on SpaceX’s major mobile carrier ambitions
item.description: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network here on Earth. As part of its plans to rival AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, SpaceX has inked a deal with Qualcomm , which will deploy its cellular technology across tens of thousands of 5G cell sites starting in 2027. SpaceX is also reportedly in talks to buy Boost Mobile , potentially allowing it to launch Starlink Mobile through the service. Another report suggests SpaceX may tap into 80,000 cell sites across the US to build out its network. SpaceX’s big plans have garnered some reactions in the telecom industry. Tim Höttges, the CEO of T-Mobile’s parent company Deutsche Telekom, said he takes SpaceX’s plans “super serious” but that it could cost Musk more than $200 billion to pull off. Follow along for the latest updates on Starlink’s major mobile carrier ambitions. What will it take for SpaceX to launch its “major” mobile network? item.title: Ships loiter near subsea cables amid Iran's warnings to Trump
item.description: Several tanker ships linked to Iran have been loitering over subsea Internet cables in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz—a possible indication that the Iranian government is preparing to attack such undersea infrastructure in response to any renewed US and Israeli strikes. The movements of three sanctioned tankers and an Iranian fishing boat have been tracked near major undersea cables by the maritime intelligence firm Windward in October, according to the Financial Times . Six active cables currently cross through the contested Strait of Hormuz, linking the Middle East to Europe, Africa and Asia, with two more cables having segments under construction in the region. Four countries, including Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar, depend entirely upon such subsea telecommunications connections running through the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint to link with the outside world. But other countries also depend heavily on the region's undersea cable network—one third of India’s westbound Internet traffic goes through the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. Read full article Comments

item.title: All Happy Mask Shop buyer locations in Zelda Ocarina of Time
item.description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's Happy Mask Shop quest sends you around Hyrule peddling masks to specific customers. That sounds like a cushy gig, except you have very little guidance about who your customers are, and you occasionally even have to pay back the cost of the mask, too. However, if you want a big chunk of cash and a chance to see and hear everything in Ocarina of Time , it's worth the hassle.
